(14.2.47.c) He is the restorer of that which was dislocated. (14.2.47.c) He is the restorer of that which was dislocated. (14.2.47.c)
May the darkness depart from us—the dark blue, the tawny, and the red.
That burning *pṛṣātakī* plant, I fasten it upon this wooden post.
As many spells (*kṛtyā*) as there are on the undergarment, as many snares as belong to King Varuṇa—[I bind them all here].
(14.2.49.c) Whatever failures and whatever misfortunes are in this [garment], those I place upon this sacrificial post.
(14.2.50’) That body of mine which is most dear has become afraid of the garment;
O Lord of the Forest, place its hem (*nīvi*) in front, so that we may not come to harm. (50) {11}

Whatever ends, however many threads, whatever warp-ends and whatever woof-threads there are— may that garment woven by the wives touch us with comfort. 51 These longing young maidens, going from the world of the fathers to their husband—
(14.2.52.c) They have released the consecration; Svāhā!
||52|| (14.2.53’) Released by Bṛhaspati, the All-Gods have sustained it.
(14.2.53.c) That luster which has entered into the cows—with that we unite this [woman]. ||53||
Released by Bṛhaspati, the Viśvedevas have sustained it;
that brilliance which has entered into the cows—with that we unite this [earth]. 54.
Released by Bṛhaspati, the Viśvedevas have sustained it. 55.
(14.2.55.c) That which has entered into the cattle as *bhajas*, with that we unite this [earth].
(14.2.56’) Released by Bṛhaspati, the All-Gods have sustained it;
(14.2.56.c) that glory which has entered into the cattle, with that we unite this [earth].
Released by Bṛhaspati, the All-Gods sustained it;
that milk which has entered into the cows—with that we unite this [earth].
Released by Bṛhaspati, the All-Gods sustained it.

(14.2.58.c) Whatever essence has entered into the cows—with that we unite this [person]. ||58|| (14.2.59’) If these long-haired people have danced together in your house, causing harm with their wailing;
(14.2.59.c) may Agni and Savitṛ release you from that sin. ||59||

If this daughter of yours, with disheveled hair, wept in the house, bringing evil with her weeping—may Agni and Savitṛ release you from that sin. (60) If the female relatives, the young women, danced together in your house, bringing evil with their weeping—[may Agni and Savitṛ release you from that sin]. (61)
(14.2.61.c) May Agni and Savitṛ release you from that sin.

||61|| Whatever evil has been committed by evildoers against your offspring, your cattle, or what has been established within your houses— (14.2.62.c) may Agni and Savitṛ release you from that sin. ||62||
(14.2.63) This noble woman, scattering grains of parched rice, speaks thus:
"May my husband be long-lived; may he live for a hundred autumns.
(14.2.64) Indra, bring these two together here like a pair of ruddy geese, husband and wife.
(14.2.64.c) May these two, through progeny, reach a full lifespan and enjoy all life, remaining well-established.
(14.2.65’) Whatever [malevolent rite] was performed upon the couch, upon the pillow, or upon the seat,
whatever spell they wrought at the wedding— upon the washing-stone, that we now lay down.
Whatever ill-deed, whatever impurity there is in the wedding, and whatever in the bridal procession—
on the blanket of Saṃbala we wipe away that misfortune.
Having deposited our impurity on Saṃbala and our misfortune on the blanket, [we are cleansed].
(14.2.67.c) We have become worthy of sacrifice, purified; may he prolong our lifespans.
67 (14.2.68’) This artificial thorn, which has a hundred teeth—let it scrape away the impurity from her hair and the impurity from her head. 68
From limb by limb we drive the consumption out of her.
Let it not reach the earth nor the gods; let it not reach the sky nor the vast intermediate space.
Let it not reach the waters, for they are impurity, O Agni; let it not reach Yama nor all the ancestors.
I bind you together with the milk of the earth; I bind you together with the milk of the plants.
I bind you together with offspring and wealth; thus bound, win for us this prize. I am he, you are she.
I am the *sāman*, you are the *ṛc*. I am heaven, you are the earth.
(14.2.71.c) Let us two come together here; let us procreate offspring.
(14.2.72’) May our sons be born with precedence; may the liberal givers desire sons for us. (14.2.72.c) Unharmed, let us be united for the winning of great booty.
(14.2.73) Those ancestors who have come to this bridal procession as beholders of the bride— may they grant protection, rich in progeny, to this bride who is now united with her husband.
(14.2.74) Those who came here of old, acting as the girdle [of the sacrifice], having bestowed upon her here offspring and wealth—
(14.2.74.c) Let them carry her along the path of one who has not yet departed; this Virāj, possessing good offspring, has conquered.
||74|| (14.2.75’) Wake up, O well-awakened one, being awakened for long life lasting a hundred autumns!
(14.2.75.c) Go to the house so that you may be the mistress of the house; Savitṛ shall grant you a long life. ||75|| {14}
(15.1.1’) There was a Vrātya even as he was being impelled; he set Prajāpati in motion.
(15.1.2’) That Prajāpati beheld gold within himself; he brought that forth. (15.1.3’) That became one; that became marked with a spot; that became great; that became the eldest. That—
(15.1.3.c) That became Brahman; that became ascetic fervor; that became truth; through that he was born.
3 (15.1.4’) He grew; he became great; he became Mahādeva.
4 (15.1.5’) He went around to the lordship of the gods; he became Īśāna. 5
He was a solitary Vratya; he took up a bow, which was indeed the bow of Indra. Its belly is blue and its back is red.
"With the blue he veils his unpleasant rival, and with the red he pierces him who hates him," so say the exponents of sacred knowledge.
(15.1.1) He arose; he moved forth toward the eastern direction.
(15.1.2) The Bṛhat and the Rathantara [Sāmans], and the Ādityas and the Viśve Devas, followed after him.
(15.1.3) He who, knowing this, [assails] a Vrātya, assails the Bṛhat and the Rathantara, and the Ādityas and the Viśve Devas.
He who knows this does not revile anyone.
3. He becomes the beloved abode of the Bṛhat and the Rathantara, of the Ādityas, and of the Viśvedevas—he who knows thus.

In the eastern direction of that [chariot] is Faith, the unchaste woman; Mitra is the charioteer; discernment is the seat; the day is the turban; the night is the hair; the two green [reins] are the side-locks; the jewel is the glittering ornament.
(5) Both the past and the future are the attendants; the mind is the path. (6)
Mātariśvan and Pavamāna are the two who carry him along the paths; Vāta is the charioteer, Reṣman is the whip, and Kīrti and Yaśas are the two precursors.
(7) Fame comes to him and glory comes to him who knows this. (8) [1]
He rose up; he moved toward the southern direction.
After him followed the Yajñāyajñīya and the Vāmadevya, as well as the sacrifice, the sacrificer, and the cattle.
He who knows this cuts himself off from the Yajñāyajñīya, from the Vāmadevya, from the sacrifice, from the sacrificer, and from the cattle.
He censures the Vratya together with the *vāmadevya*.
To his south is Uṣas the harlot; the mantra is her garment, the Māgadha her dress, the day her turban, the night her hair, the two green ones her earrings, and the *kalmali* plant her jewel.
The new moon and the full moon are her attendants, and the mind is her carriage.
(15.1.14.c) Mātariśvan and Pavamāna are the two who carry him along the paths; Vāta is the charioteer, and Reṣman is the whip; Kīrti and Yaśas are the two precursors.
(15.1.14.e) Fame comes to him and glory comes to him who knows this. 14. [2] (15.1.15’) He arose and moved forth toward the western direction. 15.
Vairūpa, Vairāja, the Waters, and King Varuṇa followed after him.
He who speaks ill of a Vrātya who knows this cuts himself off from Vairūpa, Vairāja, the Waters, and King Varuṇa.

He who knows this becomes the beloved abode of Vairūpa, Vairāja, of the waters, and of King Varuṇa. (15.1.18) In his western direction, a courtesan is the sacrificial fee; laughter is the Magadhan bard; knowledge is the garment; the day is the turban; the night is the hair; two green ear-rings are the earrings; and a glittering gem is the jewel. (15.1.19)
Day and night are the attendants; the mind is the carriage-pole.
Mātariśvan and Pavamāna are the two who draw the carriage-pole; Vāta is the charioteer, and Reṣman is the whip. Renown and glory are the two precursors.
Renown comes to him, and glory comes to him, who knows thus. 20. [3]
He rose up; he moved forth toward the northern direction.
After him, the Śyaita and the Naudhasa, the Seven Seers, and King Soma moved forth.
He who knows this and yet harms a Vrātya cuts himself off from the Śyaita, the Naudhasa, the Seven Seers, and King Soma.
He does not revile him.
||23|| He who knows this becomes dear to the abode of the Śyaita, the Naudhasa, the Seven Seers, and King Soma.

In his northern direction are lightning as his courtesan and thunder as his bard; discernment is his garment, day his turban, night his hair, and the two seasons his earrings; the *kalmaṣa* gem is his crest-jewel.
Both learning and renown are his attendants, and the mind is his carriage-path.
Mātariśvan and Pavamāna are the two who carry him along the path; Vāta is the charioteer and Reṣman is the whip.
Fame and glory are the two precursors.
(27) Fame comes to him and glory comes to him, whoever knows this thus. (28) [4]
(15.3.1) He stood upright for a year. The gods said to him, "Vrātya, why do you stand?
(15.3.2) He replied, "Let them bring me a throne.
(15.3.3) They brought a throne for that Vrātya.
(15.3.4) Her two forefeet were summer and spring, and her two hindfeet were autumn and the rainy season.
(15.3.5) The *bṛhat* and the *rathaṃtara* were the two longitudinal beams, and the *yajñāyajñiya* and the *vāmadevya* were the two cross-beams.
(15.3.6) The *ṛc*-verses were the warp-threads running eastward, and the *yajus*-formulas were the woof-threads running crosswise.
The Veda is the covering, the Brahman is the cushion; the Sāman is the seat, the Udgītha the support. The Vrātya ascended that throne.

The divine folk were his attendants; his intentions were the sacrificial assistants (*prahāyyāḥ*); all beings were his subordinates (*upasadaḥ*). (10) All beings indeed become his subordinates for him who knows thus.
(11) To him [came] from the eastern direction... (1)
(15.3.2) They made the two months of spring his guardians, and the Bṛhat and Rathantara [Sāmans] his attendants.
(15.3.3) The two months of spring guard him from the eastern quarter, and the Bṛhat and Rathantara attend upon him, for one who knows thus.
(15.3.4) For him [they made guardians] from the southern quarter.
(15.3.5) They made the two summer months the guardians, and the *yajñāyajñiya* and the *vāmadevya* the performers of the ritual service.
(15.3.6) The two summer months protect him from the southern quarter and the *yajñāyajñiya* and the *vāmadevya* attend upon him, for one who knows thus.
To him, they made the two months of the rainy season the guardians from the western direction, and the Vairūpa and Vairāja [Sāmans] the attendants.
The two months of the rainy season guard him from the western direction, and the Vairūpa and Vairāja attend upon him, for one who knows thus. [3]
From that northern direction, they made the two autumn months his guardians, and the Śyaita and Naudhasa chants his attendants.
The two autumn months guard him from the northern direction, and the Śyaita and Naudhasa chants attend upon him, for one who knows thus. [4]
For him, they made the two winter months the guardians of the fixed quarter; the earth and Agni were the attendants.
The two winter months guard him from the fixed quarter, and the earth and Agni attend upon him, for one who knows thus. [5]
For him, they made the two months of the cold season the guardians of the upward direction, and the sky and the sun the attendants.
The two months of the cold season guard him from the upward direction, and the sky and the sun attend upon him, for whoever knows thus. [6]
(15.3.1) For him, they made Bhava the archer, the follower, from the intermediate region of the eastern quarter.
(15.3.2) Bhava, the archer, stands as a follower from the intermediate region of the eastern quarter for this man.
(15.3.3) Neither Śarva, nor Bhava, nor Īśāna harms him, nor his cattle, nor his kinsmen, who knows thus.
(15.3.4) For him, they made Śarva, the archer, the follower from the intermediate region of the southern quarter.

(15.3.5) Śarva, the archer, as a follower stands by him from the intermediate region of the southern quarter; neither Śarva, nor Bhava, nor Īśāna harms him, nor his cattle, nor his kin, who knows thus. [2]
(15.3.6) For him, they made Paśupati the archer the follower from the intermediate region of the western quarter.

(15.3.7) Paśupati the archer, as a follower, stands by him from the intermediate region of the western quarter; neither Śarva, nor Bhava, nor Īśāna harms him, nor his cattle, nor his kinsmen, for one who knows thus. [3]
(15.3.8) For him, from the intermediate region of the northern direction, they made the fierce god, the archer, the follower.

(15.3.9) The fierce god, the archer, as a follower, stands by him from the intermediate region of the northern direction; neither Śarva, nor Bhava, nor Īśāna harms him, nor his cattle, nor his kinsmen, for one who knows thus.
(15.3.10) For him, from the intermediate region of the fixed (dhruvā) direction, they made Rudra, the archer, the follower.
(15.3.11) Rudra, the archer, stands behind him from the intermediate region of the fixed quarter; neither Śarva, nor Bhava, nor Īśāna harms him, his cattle, or his kinsmen—he who knows thus. 11.
(15.3.12) For him, they made Mahādeva, the archer, the one who stands behind from the intermediate region of the upward quarter. 12.

(15.3.13) Mahādeva, the archer, follows him from the intermediate region of the upward direction as his pursuer. Neither Śarva, nor Bhava, nor Īśāna harms him, nor his cattle, nor his kinsmen, for one who knows thus.
(15.3.14) For him, they made Īśāna the archer the pursuer from all the intermediate regions.
(15.3.15’) Īśāna, the archer, follows him from all intermediate directions as he stands firm.
(15.3.16’) Neither Śarva, nor Bhava, nor Īśāna harms his cattle or his kinsmen, provided he knows this.
[7] (15.3.1’) He moved out toward the fixed direction.
The earth, the fire, the herbs, the trees, the forest products, and the creepers followed after him.
He who knows this becomes the beloved abode of the earth, the fire, the herbs, the trees, the forest products, and the creepers. [1]
(15.3.4) He moved out toward the upward direction. (15.3.5) After him, Right and Truth, the Sun and the Moon, and the Nakṣatras moved out.
(15.3.6) Of Right and of Truth, of the Sun and of the Moon, and of the Nakṣatras—

(15.3.6.c) He who knows this becomes a beloved abode. 6. [2] (15.3.7’) He moved forth toward the northern direction. 7. (15.3.8’) The *ṛc*s, the *sāmans*, the *yajus* formulas, and the sacred word (*brahman*) followed after him as he moved. 8.
(15.3.9) He who knows this becomes the beloved abode of the *ṛc*s, the *sāmans*, the *yajus* formulas, and the Brahman. 9.
(15.3.10) He moved forth toward the northern direction (*bṛhatī diś*). 10. (15.3.11) After him followed the *itihāsas*, the *purāṇas*, the *gāthās*, and the *nārāśaṃsīs*. 11.
He who knows this becomes the beloved abode of history, of the Purāṇa, of the Gāthās, and of the Nārāśaṃsīs. 12.
He moved forth toward the highest direction. 13.
The Āhavanīya fire, the Gārhapatya fire, the Dakṣiṇāgni fire, the sacrifice, the sacrificer, and the cattle followed after him. 14.
He who knows this becomes the beloved abode of the Āhavanīya, the Gārhapatya, the Dakṣiṇāgni, the sacrifice, the sacrificer, and the cattle. 15. [5]
He set out toward an unassigned direction.
The seasons and the seasonal phenomena, the worlds and the world-dwellers, the months and the half-months, and day and night followed after him.
Indeed, he [became] the essence of the seasons and the seasonal phenomena, of the worlds and the world-dwellers, of the months and the half-months, and of day and night.
He who knows this becomes the abode of glory. 18.
He moved forth toward the direction from which there is no return; he thought, "From there I shall not return. 19.
Diti, Aditi, Iḍā, and Indrāṇī followed after him. 20.
He becomes the beloved abode of Diti, Aditi, Iḍā, and Indrāṇī—he who knows thus.
(15.3.21) He moved forth along the quarters; after him Virāj moved forth, as did all the gods and all the deities.
(15.3.22) He becomes the beloved abode of Virāj, of all the gods, and of all the deities—he who knows thus. (15.3.23)
[8] He moved along through all the intermediate regions.
Prajāpati, Parameṣṭhin, the father, and the grandfather followed after him.
He who knows this becomes the beloved abode of Prajāpati, of Parameṣṭhin, of his father, and of his grandfather.
That greatness, having become a good mountain, went to the end of the earth; it became the ocean.
Prajāpati, Parameṣṭhin, his father, and his grandfather, as well as the waters and faith, having become rain, turned back toward it.
Water goes to him, faith goes to him, and rain goes to him who knows this.
Faith, sacrifice, the world, food, and the eating of food— having become these— revolve around him.
Faith comes to him, sacrifice comes to him, the world comes to him, food comes to him, and the eating of food comes to him—he who knows this thus.
He took delight; from that, the Rājanya was born.
He rose up toward the people, his kinsmen, food, and the means of eating.
He who knows this becomes the beloved abode of the people, of his kinsmen, of food, and of the means of eating. He moved forth among the people.
The assembly hall, the council, the army, and the heroes followed after him.
He who knows this becomes the beloved abode of the assembly hall, the council, the army, and the heroes.
Now, if a Vrātya who possesses such knowledge should come as a guest to the house of a king—
(15.10.2) One should honor him as superior to oneself; thus one does not bring harm upon the *kṣatra*, nor does one bring harm upon the kingdom.
(15.10.3) From that very source, indeed, the *brahman* and the *kṣatra* arose. They said, "Into whom shall we enter? (15.10.4) [They replied:
"Let the *brahman* enter Bṛhaspati, and let the *kṣatra* enter Indra; so it shall be."
(15.10.5) Therefore, the sacred power (*brahman*) indeed entered Bṛhaspati, and the ruling power (*kṣatra*) entered Indra.
(15.10.6) This earth, indeed, is Bṛhaspati; the sky is Indra.
(15.10.7) This fire, indeed, is the sacred power; yonder sun is the ruling power.
(15.10.8) Sacred knowledge comes to him; he becomes endowed with the splendor of sacred knowledge. (15.10.9) He who knows the earth as Bṛhaspati and as Agni [attains this].
(15.10.10) Spiritual power comes to him; he becomes possessed of spiritual power.
(15.10.11’) He who knows the Āditya as the ruling power (*kṣatra*), the heaven, and Indra.

‖11‖ (15.11.1’) Now, if a Vrātya who knows this should come as a guest to one’s house— ‖1‖ (15.11.2’) One should rise up toward him personally and say: “Vrātya, where have you stayed? Vrātya, here is water; Vrātya, let them satisfy you; Vrātya, [do] as is dear to you. ‖2‖
"Let it be so, Vrātya, as your will desires; let it be so, Vrātya, as your wish desires.
(15.11.3) When he says to him, "Vrātya, where did you stay?", he thereby secures for himself the paths traveled by the gods.
(15.11.4) When he says to him, "Vrātya, [drink] water," he thereby secures for himself the waters.
When he says to him, "O Vrātya, may they satisfy you," he thereby makes his breath more abundant.
(6) When he says to him, "O Vrātya, let it be as is dear to you," he thereby obtains what is dear.
(7) What is dear comes to him; he becomes dear to what is dear, he who knows thus. (8)
(15.11.8) When he says to him, "O Vrātya, let it be as your will," he thereby secures his very will.
(15.11.9) Will comes to him; he becomes the master of masters who knows thus.
(15.11.10) When he says to him, "O Vrātya, let it be as your desire," he thereby secures his very desire.
Desire comes to him, and he attains his desire, who knows this thus.

Now, if a Vrātya who knows this should come as a guest to the house of someone whose fires have been taken out and into whom the Agnihotra oblation has been placed, [the host] should rise up toward him in person and say: "O Vrātya, grant me leave; I shall offer the sacrifice."
He may either grant permission and offer the oblation, or he may neither grant permission nor offer the oblation.
He who offers the oblation having been granted permission by a Vrātya who knows thus,
knows the path leading to the fathers and the path leading to the gods.

(15.12.6) Among the gods, he does not cut off [the offering]; his oblation becomes accepted. (15.12.7) His abode remains in this world for him who offers having been permitted by a Vrātya who knows thus. (15.12.8) But he who offers without being permitted by a Vrātya who knows thus—[his abode is not preserved]. (15.12.8) Now, as for him who offers without being permitted by a Vrātya who knows thus...

He knows neither the path of the fathers nor the path of the gods. He is cut off from the gods; his offering becomes as if unoffered. No abode remains for him in this world who offers while not authorized by a Vrātya who possesses such knowledge.
(15.12.1) Therefore, when a Vrātya who knows this stays as a guest in someone’s house for one night;
(15.12.2) by that, he wins those worlds on earth which are meritorious.
(15.12.3) Therefore, when a Vrātya who knows this stays as a guest in someone’s house for a second night;
(15.12.4) Those worlds that are meritorious in the intermediate space—verily, those he wins by that.
4. (15.12.5) Therefore, when a Vrātya who knows this stays as a guest in one’s house for the third night— (15.12.6) Those worlds that are meritorious in heaven—verily, those he wins by that. 6.
Thus, for whomever a Vrātya who knows this stays as a guest in his house on the fourth night,
he wins those worlds which are the most excellent among the excellent.
[4] Thus, for whomever a Vrātya who knows this stays as a guest in his house for an unlimited number of nights...
(15.12.10) He thereby wins those very worlds of immeasurable merit.

||10|| [5] (15.12.11) Now, if a Vrātya who calls himself a Vrātya should come as a guest to one's house under that name, ||11|| [6] (15.12.12) One should either drive him away or one should not drive him away. ||12|| [7]
"Let us beg water from this deity; let us clothe this deity; I envelop this deity. Having thus enveloped it, he should proceed.
(15.12.14) For him who knows thus, that offering becomes made in that very deity. (15.12.14) [9]
(15.12.1) When he moved out toward the eastern direction, he moved out having become the host of Maruts, having made the mind the eater of food.
(15.12.2) He who knows this eats food with the mind as the eater of food.
(15.12.3) When he moved out toward the southern direction, he moved out having become strength, having made it the eater of food.
(15.12.4) He who knows thus eats food by means of the eater of food through strength.

(15.12.5) When he moved forth toward the western quarter, he moved forth having become King Varuṇa, making the waters the eaters of food. (15.12.6) He who knows thus eats food by means of the waters that are eaters of food.

When he moved toward the northern direction, he moved having become King Varuṇa, with the seven seers, having made the oblation into food for eating. ||7|| He who knows thus eats food through the oblation that is food for eating. ||8|| [4]
When he moved toward the fixed quarter, he moved having become Viṣṇu, making Virāj the eater of food.
9. He who knows thus eats food by means of Virāj as the eater of food.
10. When he moved toward the cattle, he moved having become Rudra, making the plants the eaters of food. 11.
He who knows this eats food by means of plants that provide food.
(15.12.12) When he moved out after the ancestors, he moved out having become King Yama, having made the utterance *svadhā* the eater of food.
(15.12.13) He who knows this eats food by means of the utterance *svadhā*, which is the eater of food. (15.12.14)
When he moved forth among men, he moved forth having become Agni, making the *svāhā*-utterance the eater of food.
He who knows thus eats food by means of the *svāhā*-utterance as the eater of food.
When he moved forth toward the upward direction, he moved forth having become Bṛhaspati, making the *vaṣaṭ*-utterance the eater of food.
He who knows this eats food through the *vaṣaṭ*-call, which is the eater of food.

(15.12.18) When he moved out after the gods, having become the Ruler (*īśāna*), he moved out after them, making Wrath (*manyu*) the eater of food. (15.12.19) He who knows this eats food through Wrath, which is the eater of food. (15.12.20)
When he moved forth after the creatures, he moved forth having become Prajāpati, having made breath the eater of food.
He who knows thus eats food by means of breath as the eater of food.
When he moved forth after all the intermediate regions, he moved forth having become Parameṣṭhin, having made Brahman the eater of food.
He who knows thus eats food through the Brahman that devours food. ||24|| [12] Of that Vratya:
there are seven out-breaths, seven in-breaths, and seven diffused breaths. ||2||
Of that Vrātya:
that which is his first upward breath, named *ūrdhva*, is this Agni.
Of that Vrātya.
(15.15.4.c) His second vital breath, named Prauḍha, is that Āditya. (15.15.5’) Of that Vrātya: (15.15.5.c) His third vital breath, named Abhyūḍha, is that Candramas.
Of that Vrātya:
his fourth vital breath, named Vibhū, is this Pavamāna.
Of that Vrātya.
(15.15.7.c) That which is his fifth vital breath, named *yoni*, is these waters.
||7|| Of that Vrātya:
(15.15.8.c) that which is his sixth vital breath, named *priya*, is these domestic animals. ||8||
Of that Vrātya— (15.15.9.c)—
that which is his seventh breath, named Aparimita, those are his offspring.
||9|| Of that Vrātya— (15.16.1.a)— [of that Vrātya].
(15.16.1.c) That which is his first downward breath is the full moon day.
(15.16.2’) Of that Vrātya,
(15.16.2.c) that which is his second downward breath is the Aṣṭakā.
Of that Vrātya:
his third downward breath is the New Moon (Amāvāsyā).
Of that Vrātya...
(15.16.4.c) That which is his fourth downward breath is faith.
(15.16.5.a) Of that Vrātya:
(15.16.5.c) that which is his fifth downward breath is initiation.
Of that Vrātya:
that which is his sixth downward breath (*apāna*) is the sacrifice.
Of that Vrātya...

(15.16.7.c) That which is his seventh downward breath (*apāna*)—these are the sacrificial gifts (*dakṣiṇās*). 7. (15.17.1’) Of that Vratya: (15.17.1.c) That which is his first diffused breath (*vyāna*)—this is the earth. 1.
Of that Vrātya:
(15.17.2.c) that which is his second *vyāna* is the intermediate space.
Of that Vrātya: (15.17.3) [that which is his third *apāna* is the earth.]
(15.17.3.c) That which is his third diffused breath (*vyāna*) is the sky. 3. Of that *vrātya*: (15.17.4.c) That which is his fourth diffused breath (*vyāna*) is those constellations (*nakṣatra*). 4.
Of that Vrātya:
(15.17.5.c) that which is his fifth vital breath (*vyāna*) is the seasons.
5. Of that Vrātya:
(15.17.6.c) That which is his sixth *vyāna* is the seasons (*ṛtu*).
(15.17.7’) Of that *vrātya*:
(15.17.7.c) That which is his seventh *vyāna* is the year (*saṃvatsara*).
Of that Vrātya:
(15.17.8.c) "The gods go around him for a common purpose; indeed, the seasons go around the year and the Vrātya.
Of that Vrātya: (15.17.9) [the same applies].
When they enter into the sun on both the new moon day and the full moon day—
of that *vrātya*,
this is their one immortality: namely, the oblation itself.
(15.18.1) Of that Vrātya:
(15.18.2) That which is his right eye is yonder sun; that which is his left eye is yonder moon.
(15.18.3) That which is his right ear is this Agni; that which is his left ear is this Pavamāna.
Day and night are the two nostrils; Diti and Aditi are the two skull-bones of the head; the year is the head.
(15.18.5) By day the Vrātya faces west, by night he faces east; homage to the Vrātya! (16.1.1) Released is the bull of the waters; released are the celestial fires. (16.1.1)
(16.1.2’) Crushing, crushing all around, grinding, grinding to pieces;
(16.1.3’) Mroka, Manohā, Khana, Nirdāha, Ātmadūṣin, Tanūdūṣin;
(16.1.4’) this one I cast away beyond him; do not let him descend upon me.
(16.1.5’) By that [means], we cast it upon him who hates us and whom we hate.
(16.1.6’) You are the foremost of the waters; I release you into the ocean.
(16.1.7’) Whatever fire is in the waters, I cast beyond it—the lurking one, the digger, the defiler of the body.
(16.1.8) Or that fire which has entered into the waters—this is it; whatever is terrible among you, that is this. (16.1.9) May he consecrate you with the power of Indra.
(16.1.10) O stainless waters, carry away defilement from us.
(16.1.11) May they carry away our sin from us; may they carry away our evil dreams.
(16.1.12) Behold me with a gracious eye, O Waters; touch my skin with your gracious body.
(16.1.13) We invoke the auspicious fires that dwell in the waters; O goddesses, bestow upon me sovereign power and splendor.
(16.2.1’) Away with ill-will! May my speech be full of vigor and sweetness.
(16.2.2’) You are full of sweetness; may I utter sweet speech.
(16.2.3’) Invoked by me is the protector; invoked is the protection.
(16.2.4) May my ears hear well; may my ears hear auspiciously; may I hear an auspicious report.
(16.2.5) May good hearing and attentive listening not abandon me; may the eye of Suparṇa be eternal light.
(16.2.6) You are the sacrificial grass-bundle of the seers; homage be to the divine grass-bundle.
May I be the head of riches; may I be the head of my equals.
(1) May Ruja and Vena not desert me; may Mūrdhan and Vidharma not desert me.
(2) May Urva and Camasa not desert me; may Dhartar and Dharuṇa not desert me. (3)
May Vimoka and Mārdrapavi not desert me; may Ārdradānu and Mātariśvan not desert me.
(5) Bṛhaspati is my self, named Nṛmaṇas, dear to the heart. (6) My heart is free from distress; wide is my pasture; by my sustaining power, I am the ocean. (7)
May I be the navel of riches, may I be the navel of my equals.
(1) You are a good seat, a bringer of prosperity, immortal among mortals.
(2) May the out-breath not desert me; may the in-breath not depart, leaving me behind. (3)
May Sūrya protect me from the day, Agni from the earth, Vāyu from the intermediate space, Yama from men, and Sarasvatī from earthly beings.
May out-breath and in-breath not desert me; may I not perish among the people.
May there be well-being today from the dawns and the nights. May I attain all the waters with my whole troop.

(16.4.7) You are the Śakvarī verses; may cattle come to me. May Mitra and Varuṇa grant me out-breath and in-breath; may Agni bestow skill upon me. (16.5.7) We know your origin, O Sleep: you are the son of Grāhi, the agent of Yama. We know your origin, O Sleep: you are the son of Nirṛti, the agent of Yama.
(16.5.7.c) You are the ender; you are death.
(16.5.7.e) O Dream, we know you as such; therefore, O Dream, protect us from bad dreams.
(16.5.7’) We know your origin, O Dream: you are the son of Non-existence, the agent of Yama.
(16.5.7.c) You are the ender; you are death.
(16.5.7.e) O dream, we know you as such; therefore, O dream, protect us from bad dreams.
(16.5.7’) We know your origin, O dream: you are the son of Destruction, the instrument of Yama.
(16.5.7.c) You are the Ender; you are Death.
(16.5.7.e) O Dream, we know you as such; protect us, O Dream, from evil dreaming.
(16.5.7’) We know your origin, O Dream: you are the son of Destruction, the agent of Yama.
(16.5.7.c) You are the ender; you are death.
(16.5.7.e) O dream, we know you as such; protect us, O dream, from bad dreaming!
7 (16.5.7’) We know your origin, O dream: you are the son of the sisters of the gods, the agent of Yama. 8
(16.6.1) We have conquered today; we have sat down today; we are now free from sin.
(16.6.2) O Uṣas, may that evil dream from which we were afraid be dispelled by your light.
(16.6.3) Carry it away to our enemy; carry it away to the one who curses us.
(16.6.4) To him whom we hate and him who hates us—to him we send this.
(16.6.5) The goddess Dawn, in harmony with Speech; the goddess Speech, in harmony with Dawn.
(16.6.6) The Lord of Dawn, in harmony with the Lord of Speech; [the Lord of Dawn], in harmony with the Lord of Speech.
(16.6.7) May they carry away to that [place] the stingy ones, the ill-named ones, and the Sadānvās. (16.6.8) The Kumbhīkas, the Dūṣīkas, and the Pīyakas.
(16.6.9) The evil dream while awake, the evil dream in sleep.

(16.6.10) From the boons that do not come, from the unfulfilled intentions, and from the snares of malice that do not release—(16.6.11) O Agni, may the gods carry that away to yonder world, so that he may become like a useless, unstable, and ineffective beast of burden.
(16.7.1) With that [missile] I pierce him; with non-existence I pierce him; with destruction I pierce him; with utter ruin I pierce him; with seizure I pierce him. Ta!
With butter I pierce him.
(16.7.2) With the terrible and cruel commands of the gods I urge him on.
(16.7.3) Into the two jaws of Vaiśvānara I place him. (16.7.4)
(16.7.4’) Thus, let her swallow him who is not such.
(16.7.5’) May his own self hate him who hates us; may he whom we hate hate himself.
(16.7.6’) We drive the hater out from heaven, out from earth, out from the intermediate space.

And Suyāma, the son of Cakṣus. ||7|| Here, I wipe away this evil dream upon the grandson of such-and-such and the son of such-and-such. ||8|| Whatever I have encountered here and there, whatever at night, or during the earlier part of the night. ||9||
Whether I am awake or asleep, whether by day or by night, whatever I encounter day after day—from that [evil] protect me! Slay him; revel in that [victory]; crush his very ribs!
(16.7.13’) May he not live; may his vital breath abandon him!
(16.8.13’) Victory is ours; the breakthrough is ours; the cosmic order is ours; splendor is ours; the sacred formulation is ours; the heavenly light is ours; the sacrifice is ours;
cattle are ours; progeny is ours; heroes are ours.

Victorious are we; triumphant are we; our is the cosmic order (*ṛta*); ours is splendor; ours is the sacred word (*brahman*); ours is the heavenly light (*svar*); ours is the sacrifice; ours are the cattle; ours are the offspring; ours are the heroes.

The corpse is ours, our offspring is ours, our heroes are ours.

(16.8.13’) Victory is ours; the victory is ours; the cosmic order is ours; splendor is ours; the sacred word is ours; the heavenly light is ours; the sacrifice is ours;
cattle are ours; progeny is ours; heroes are ours. (16.8.13.c) Therefore, we exclude that one: that son of such-and-such a lineage, the son of such-and-such a woman, he who is so-and-so.
(16.8.13.e) May he not be released from the snares of the Atharvans!

cattle are ours; progeny is ours; heroes are ours.
(16.8.13.c) Therefore, we exclude that one—him, the son of such-and-such a lineage, the son of such-and-such a mother;
may he who is that one not escape the snares of the trees.
(16.8.13.e) Victory is ours, the breakthrough is ours, the cosmic order is ours, splendor is ours, the sacred formulation is ours, heaven is ours, and the sacrifice is ours. Praise is ours!
Our horses are ours, our offspring are ours, our heroes are ours. Therefore, we exclude that one—him, the son of such-and-such a lineage and such-and-such a mother, he who is so-and-so.
May he not escape from the snares of the trees.

(16.8.13.e) May he not be released from the snares of the seasons.

(16.8.13.e) May he not be released from the snares of the Ārtavāns.

May he not escape the snares of the months.

May he not be released from the snares of the half-months!
Victorious are we; triumphant are we; truth is ours; splendor is ours; sacred formulation is ours; heaven is ours; sacrifice is ours;
cattle are ours; progeny is ours; heroes are ours.

Our horses are ours, our offspring are ours, our heroes are ours.
Therefore, we exclude that one—him who belongs to such-and-such a lineage, the son of such-and-such a woman;
may he not escape from the bonds while day and night are joined together.

Our horses are ours, our offspring are ours, our heroes are ours.

(16.9.1) Victory is ours; triumph is ours; I have overcome all hostile armies.
(16.9.2) This Agni has declared, and Soma has declared it: may Pūṣan place me in the world of the well-performed deed.
(16.9.3) We have gone to the light; we have gone to the light of heaven; we have united with the light of Sūrya.
(16.9.4’) For the sake of greater prosperity, may the sacrifice be rich in wealth; may I win wealth; may I become wealthy; bestow wealth upon me!

‖4‖ (17.1.1’) [I praise] the all-conquering, the subduing, the victorious, the more powerful one—him who overcomes, who has won through might, who has won the light of heaven, who has won the cattle, and who has won all gathered riches.
(17.1.1.e) I invoke Indra by his name, the Worthy of Praise: may I be long-lived. (17.1.2’) [I invoke] the overcomer, the subduer, the victorious, the more powerful;
the one who subdues, the winner of strength, the winner of heaven, the winner of cattle, the winner of all wealth.

(17.1.2.e) I invoke Indra by his name, the One to be Praised; may I be dear to the gods. (2) (17.1.3’) The subduer, the conqueror, the victorious, the more powerful one— (17.1.3.c) The subduing one, the winner of strength, the winner of heaven, the winner of cattle, the winner of all wealth.
(17.1.3.e) I invoke Indra by his name "Worthy of Praise" (īḍya); may I be dear to all creatures. ||3|| (17.1.4’) [I invoke] the subduer, the one who overcomes, the victorious, the most powerful;
(17.1.4.c) the one who conquers, the winner of strength, the winner of heaven, the winner of cattle, the winner of wealth.
(17.1.4.e) I invoke Indra, whose name is to be praised; may I become beloved among cattle. (17.1.5’) [I invoke] the overcomer, the subduer, the victorious, the more powerful one;
the subduer, the winner of strength, the winner of heaven, the winner of cattle, the winner of all wealth.
(17.1.5.e) I invoke Indra by his name, the Worthy of Praise; may I be dear among my peers.
(5) (17.1.6’) Rise up, rise up, O Sūrya! Rise up toward me with splendor.
May he who hates me be overcome, and may I not be overcome by him whom I hate. O Viṣṇu, your heroic powers are manifold.
(17.1.6.e) Do you fill us with cattle of every form; place me in the nourishing highest heaven.

(17.1.7’) Rise up, rise up, O Sūrya; shine upon me with splendor! May I see those whom I have seen and those whom I have not; bestow your benevolence upon them. For yours, O Viṣṇu, are many heroic powers.
(17.1.7.e) Do thou fill us with cattle of every form; place me in the secure dwelling in the highest heaven.

(17.1.8’) Let not those snarers who stand here within the waters and the floods harm thee. Leaving behind all ill-will, thou hast ascended this heaven; as such, be gracious to us, and may we abide in thy favor. O Viṣṇu, manifold are thy heroic deeds.
(17.1.8.e) Do you fill us with cattle of every form; place me in the nourishment of the highest heaven.
8 (17.1.9’) O Indra, for our great good fortune, protect us on all sides with your unfailing nights; yours, O Viṣṇu, are manifold heroic powers.
(17.1.9.c) Do you fill us with cattle of every form; place me in the nourishment of the highest heaven. 9
O Indra, through your auspicious aids, be most propitious to us.
Ascending to the third heaven from the sky, praised for the drinking of Soma, you whose abode is dear, come for our well-being. O Viṣṇu, manifold are your heroic deeds;
grant us cattle of every form, and place me in the nourishment of the highest heaven. 10. {1}

(17.1.11’) You, O Indra, are the all-conquering, all-knowing, much-invoked; you, O Indra. (17.1.11.c) You, O Indra, further this well-invoked hymn of praise; be gracious to us, and may we abide in your favor. O Viṣṇu, yours are many heroic deeds.
(17.1.11.e) Do you fill us with cattle of every form; place me in the nourishment in the highest heaven. ||11||
(17.1.12’) You are undeceived upon heaven and upon earth; your majesty cannot be encompassed in the mid-air.
(17.1.12.c) Increasing through the undeceived sacred word (*brahman*), as such, O Indra, grant us protection in heaven. O Viṣṇu, yours are many heroic powers.
(17.1.12.e) Do you fill us with cattle of every form; place me in the nourishment in the highest heaven. 12.

(17.1.13’) That body of yours, O Indra, which is in the waters, which is on the earth, which is within the fire, and that which is yours, O Indra, in the purifying, light-finding [sun]—(17.1.13.c) with that body by which, O Indra, you have pervaded the mid-air, with that body of yours, O Indra, grant us protection. O Viṣṇu, your heroic powers are manifold;
(17.1.13.e) do you fill us with cattle of every form, and place me in the nourishing highest heaven. ||13||
(17.1.14’) O Indra, the seers, strengthening you with sacred hymns (*brahman*) and imploring you, have sat down for the sacrificial session (*sattra*). O Viṣṇu, yours are many heroic powers.

(17.1.14.c) Do you satisfy us with cattle of every form; place me in the realm of nourishment, in the highest heaven. 14 (17.1.15’) You [are] Trita; you go around the fountain that flows in a thousand streams, the assembly that finds the light of heaven. O Viṣṇu, yours are many heroic powers.
(17.1.15.c) Do you fill us with cattle of every form; place me in the nourishment in the highest heaven.

(17.1.16’) You guard the four quarters; you shine through both worlds with your flame. You stand over all these beings; as one who knows, you follow the path of *ṛta*. O Viṣṇu, manifold are your heroic deeds.
(17.1.16.e) Do thou fill us with cattle of every form; place me in the realm of nectar, in the highest heaven.

16 (17.1.17’) With five [steps] thou goest away to heat, with one hitherward; on a fair day thou goest forth, driving away the curse. O Viṣṇu, thy heroic powers are manifold. (17.1.17.c) Do thou fill us with cattle of every form; place me in the realm of nectar, in the highest heaven. 17
(17.1.18’) You are Indra; you are Mahendra; you are the world; you are Prajāpati.
(17.1.18.c) For you the sacrifice is spread out; to you they offer as they sacrifice. O Viṣṇu, yours are many heroic powers.
(17.1.18.e) Do you satisfy us with cattle of every form; place me in the nourishment in the highest heaven. ||18||
In the non-existent, the existent is established; in the existent, the being is established.
The being is placed within the future, and the future is established in the being. O Viṣṇu, manifold are your heroic powers.
Grant us wealth in the form of cattle of every kind; place me in the nourishing, supreme heaven. 19.19.19–e |||19||
(17.1.20’) “You are bright; you are radiant.
Just as you are radiant with radiance, so may I be radiant with radiance. (17.1.21’) “You are luster; you are light.”
(17.1.21.c) Just as you are radiant by your own luster, so may I shine with cattle and the splendor of Brahman.
||21|| (17.1.22’) Homage to him who is about to rise; homage to him who is rising; homage to him who has risen.
(17.1.22.c) Homage to the Virāj; homage to the Svarāj; homage to the Samrāj. ||22||
Homage to him who is setting, homage to him who is about to set, homage to him who has set;
homage to the far-shining one, homage to the self-radiant one, homage to the sovereign ruler.
This Āditya has risen up together with all-consuming heat.
(17.1.24.c) Subduing my rivals, may I not be overcome by those who hate me; for you, O Viṣṇu, possess manifold heroic powers.
(17.1.24.e) Do you provide us with cattle of every form; place me in the secure realm, in the highest heaven.
24 (17.1.25’) O Āditya, you have mounted the ship with a hundred oars for our well-being.
(17.1.25.c) O Day, carry me across; O Night, carry me completely across.
||25|| O Sūrya, you have mounted the ship with a hundred oars for our well-being. O Night, carry me across; O Day, carry me completely across. ||26||

Enveloped by the protection and armor of Prajāpati, and by the light and splendor of Kaśyapa— may I, reaching old age, possessing accomplished power, being vigorous, and living for a thousand years, move about as one who has performed good deeds.
Enveloped by the protection and armor of Brahmā, and by the light and splendor of Kaśyapa— may I [move about].
(17.1.28.c) May the divine arrows not reach me, nor those human ones that have been loosed for my slaughter.

||28|| (17.1.29’) Protected by *ṛta* and by all the seasons, protected by what has been and what is to be; (17.1.29.c) may neither evil nor death reach me; I shield myself with the waters of speech. ||29||
(17.1.30’) May Agni, my protector, guard me on every side; may the rising sun drive away the snares of death.
(17.1.30.c) As the dawns shine forth and the mountains stand firm, may a thousand vital breaths be gathered within me.
{3} (18.1.1’) Even though I have traveled far across the vast ocean, I would still turn back to my friend with friendship.
(18.1.1.c) May the wise one, meditating further upon it, take the grandson of the father onto the earth.
(18.1.2’) Your friend does not desire this friendship, since she who shares the same mark becomes of different form.
The heroic sons of the great Asura, the sustainers of heaven, have looked far and wide around.
(18.1.3) The immortals indeed desire this from you alone: that you abandon even a portion of your mortal nature.

Let your mind be fixed upon our mind; as a husband, may you enter into the body of your wife. (18.1.4) What have we not done before? And what now could we speak, professing the truth while uttering falsehood?
(18.1.4.c) The Gandharva in the waters and the watery maiden—therein is our kinship, that is our highest bond.
(18.1.5’) In the womb, the progenitor, the god Tvaṣṭṛ, the impeller of all forms, made us a husband and wife.
No one violates his ordinances; of this, both Earth and Heaven are aware.

(18.1.6) Who today yokes to the pole of Order the vigorous, impetuous, and ill-disposed bulls? Those who have arrows in their mouths, hearts that pierce, yet are sources of bliss—he who provides for their maintenance shall live.
(18.1.7) Who knows of this first day? Who has seen it? Who here can declare it?

(18.1.7.c) Great is the domain of Mitra and Varuṇa; what, O reviler, will you say to the men with your speech? (18.1.8’) The longing for Yama has come upon me, Yamī, so that we may lie together in a common womb.
Like a wife to her husband, I would yield my body; let us roll about like two chariot wheels.
They do not stand still, nor do they close their eyes—these spies of the gods who wander here.
O you who summon me, go quickly by another way; with that, tear him apart like two chariot wheels.
May he serve him night and day; may he repeatedly measure out the eye of the sun.
(18.1.10.c) By day, Yamī, who shares the same kinship as her twin with Pṛthivī, would violate the forbidden act of Yama.
(18.1.11’) Indeed, those later ages will surely come when kinsmen shall commit the forbidden act.
Press thy arm close to the bull; O fortunate one, seek another husband than me.
(18.1.12’) What is a brother if he becomes one who has no protector? And what is a sister if Destruction should come upon her?
Driven by desire, I murmur this much; unite my body with your body.
(18.1.13’) I am not your protector here, O Yamī; I will not unite my body with your body.

(18.1.13.c) "Seek your pleasures with another; your brother does not desire this for you, O fortunate one. (18.1.14’) "I would never unite my body with yours; they call it an evil thing when one approaches his own sister.
(18.1.14.c) "This is not a union of mind or heart—that I, as a brother, should lie upon the bed of my sister."
Alas, O Yama, you are indeed pitiable; neither your mind nor your heart have I discovered.
Surely another woman has embraced you, as a girth-belt encircles a yoked horse, or as a climbing vine clings to a tree.
O Yamī, surely another man has embraced you, as a climbing vine clings to a tree.
(18.1.16.c) O you, desire his mind, or he yours; establish with him a most auspicious understanding.

(18.1.17’) The poets have separated the three meters, which are manifold in form, beautiful to behold, and all-seeing; the waters, the winds, and the plants—these are set within a single world. (18.1.17.c) These are established in one world.

The bull has milked for the bull the milks of heaven by his own milking; the mighty one, undeceivable son of Aditi, knows all through his wisdom. He, the worshipful one, performs sacrifice for the worshipful seasons.
May the Gandharvī and the water-nymph whisper at the roar of the river; may she protect our mind on every side.
(18.1.19.c) May Aditi place us in the midst of what is desired; may our eldest brother speak first for us.

(18.1.20’) That very blessed, food-providing, glorious Dawn has shone forth for mankind, full of light, when they, according to the will of those who desire, have generated Agni as the Hotṛ priest for the sacrificial assembly. (18.1.20.c) {2}
Then the swift falcon brought down that far-reaching, all-seeing drop at the sacrifice;
when the Aryan tribes chose the wondrous Agni as their Hotṛ-priest, then indeed was the sage born.
O Agni, you are ever delightful to the man who prospers like a pasture, you who make the sacrifice well-performed through his oblations.
(18.1.22.c) Or when you, worthy of praise, having won the prize through many [songs], approach the zealous sage;
||22|| (18.1.23’) Raise up the two parents like a lover; the beloved one desires fortune and sends it forth from his heart.
||23|| The bearer speaks; the sacrificer performs his work well; the lord displays his power; the inspired poet trembles with thought. ||23||
O Agni, son of strength, that mortal who has proclaimed your favor becomes renowned far and wide;
bestowing nourishment and borne by his horses, he, radiant and powerful, adorns himself day after day.
Hear us, O Agni, in your dwelling-place, your common abode; yoke your swift chariot of immortality.
(18.1.25.c) Bring hither to us Heaven and Earth, the parents of the gods; let none of the gods be absent; may you be present here.
||25|| (18.1.26’) O Agni, when this divine assembly shall take place among the gods, worthy of sacrifice, O worshipful one;
and when you, O self-dependent lord, distribute treasures, grant us here our share of wealth. ||26||
Agni, the first Jātavedas, has looked upon the vanguard of the dawns; he has looked upon the days.
Following the sun, the dawns, and the rays, he has entered heaven and earth.
Agni, the first Jātavedas, has looked back upon the vanguard of the dawns; he has looked back upon the days.
(18.1.28.c) He has extended his rays in many directions toward the sun; he has stretched across heaven and earth.

(18.1.29’) Heaven and Earth, the first, become attentive through the *ṛta*, they whose speech is truth, when the god, making mortals perform sacrifice, sits down as the *hotṛ* priest, turning toward his own vital breath. (18.1.29.c) 29.
(18.1.30) The god who encompasses the gods by the Eternal Law (*ṛta*), carry our oblation, you who are foremost and wise;
smoke-bannered, bright with fuel, the joyous and eternal Hotṛ-priest, more skilled in sacrifice through his voice. 30.
(18.1.31) I praise you both for your increase—O Waters, dripping with ghee! O Heaven and Earth, you two worlds, hear me.
(18.1.31.c) When, O gods, you came to the path of the departed, may the two Parents here sharpen us with honey.
(31) (18.1.32’) When the cow’s own-turning became the immortal nectar of the god, those born from that uphold the two wide worlds.
(18.1.32.c) All the gods followed that sacrificial formula of yours, whereby the dappled one milks the heavenly ghee and water. (32)

(18.1.33) What has the King seized from us? When have we ever transgressed his decree? Who knows? For even Mitra, when he goes astray, is like a cry of reproach among the gods; there is no prize for those who fail to go [to him].
(18.1.34) Difficult to perceive therein is the name of the Immortal, when she who shares a common mark becomes manifold in form.

(18.1.34.c) O lofty Agni, protect without fail that man who honors you with kind thoughts. In that secret thought wherein the gods move together, we do not know it.
May Mitra, Aditi, and the divine Savitṛ proclaim us sinless here to Varuṇa.
O friends, let us instruct a sacred prayer for Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt.
(18.1.37.c) Let us praise him who is most heroic and bold.

(18.1.38’) For by your might you are renowned as the slayer of Vṛtra through the destruction of Vṛtra; O hero, with your bounties you surpass even the liberal patrons. (18.1.38.c) You bestow gifts beyond those of the wealthy. 38.
Like a steed, you traverse the broad earth; may the great winds blow here upon the ground for us.
May Mitra and Varuṇa, joined with Agni, release their heat here like fire in the forest.
39 Praise the renowned one who sits upon the chariot-seat of men, the king, the terrible, the slayer of enemies, the fierce. 40

(18.1.40.c) Be gracious to the singer, O Rudra, when you are praised; let them cast down your missile elsewhere than upon us. {4} (18.1.41’) Those seeking the gods invoke Sarasvatī while the sacrifice is being performed;
the doers of good deeds invoke Sarasvatī. May Sarasvatī grant desirable wealth to the donor. {41}
The ancestors invoke Sarasvatī as they approach the sacrifice with their sacrificial fees.
Having seated yourselves upon this sacred grass (*barhis*), rejoice; bestow upon us food free from disease.
O Sarasvatī, you who have come on the same chariot, O Goddess, rejoicing with the ancestors through hymns and funeral offerings (*svadhā*).
(18.1.43.c) Bestow here upon the sacrificer a portion of the *iḍ* worth a thousand, an increase of wealth.
(18.1.44’) Rise up, O fathers worthy of Soma—those below, those above, and those in the middle!
Those who have gone to the life-breath, who are harmless and knowers of the *ṛta*, may those fathers protect us in our invocations.

I have found the benevolent fathers, and the grandson, and the wide stride of Viṣṇu. Those who sit upon the sacred grass and partake of the pressed food with the funeral offering—may they be the most ready to come here.
Let this homage be paid today to the fathers, those who went before and those who followed after.
(18.1.46.c) Those who are settled in the earthly realm, or those who are now indeed in the well-favored quarters;
(18.1.47’) Mātali with the Kavyas, Yama with the Aṅgirases, Bṛhaspati strengthened by the Ṛkvans—
(18.1.47.c) Those whom the gods have strengthened and those who [have strengthened] the gods— may those fathers protect us in our invocations.
Truly, this is sweet and it is honeyed; truly, this is sharp and it is flavorful.
Indeed, no one at all can withstand Indra when he has drunk of this in battles.
He who has gone forth along the great slopes, having spied out the path for many—
(18.1.49.c) Worship with an oblation Yama, the son of Vivasvat, the king who gathers together the people.

(18.1.50’) Yama was the first to find for us the way; this pasture-land is not to be taken away from us— (18.1.50.c)—where our ancient fathers have passed away, having been born along their own paths.
(18.1.51’) O Fathers who sit upon the sacrificial grass, come hither with your aid; we have prepared these oblations for you—be pleased with them!
(18.1.51.c) Come to us with most auspicious protection, and then bestow upon us well-being, health, and freedom from harm!
(18.1.52’) Bending the knee and sitting down to the south, may all of you accept this our oblation with praise.

(18.1.52.c) O Fathers, do not harm us for anything, whatever offense we may have committed against you through our human nature. 52 (18.1.53’) Tvaṣṭṛ prepares the bridal procession for his daughter; because of this, all this world comes together.
The mother of Yama, being carried away, the great wife of Vivasvat, vanished. 53
Go forth, go forth by the ancient paths, by which your former fathers have departed.
You shall behold both kings rejoicing in the *svadhā* offering—Yama and the god Varuṇa.
Depart, go away, and creep apart from here; the fathers have prepared this world for him.
(18.1.55.c) By means of days, waters, and nights, Yama clearly grants him a dwelling place.
55 (18.1.56’) Desiring you, we kindle [the fire]; desiring you, we enkindle it. (18.1.56.c) Desiring them, bring the desiring ancestors here to eat the oblation. 56
Radiant indeed may we meditate; radiant may we kindle [thee].
O radiant one, bring the radiant ancestors here to eat the oblation.
(57) The Aṅgirases, our fathers, the Navagvas, the Atharvans, and the Bhṛgus, who are worthy of Soma— (58)
May we abide in the benevolent favor of those worthy of sacrifice, and likewise in their auspicious goodwill.
(58) Come here with the Angirases, the ones worthy of sacrifice; O Yama, rejoice here with the Vairūpas. I invoke Vivasvat, who is your father, that he may sit down upon this sacred grass. (59)
(18.1.60) Ascend this sacrificial grass-mat, O Yama, in harmony with the Aṅgirases, the fathers;
let the mantras recited by the sages carry you here, O King; rejoice in this oblation. (18.1.61) From here they have gone forth; they have ascended to the ridges of heaven.
(18.1.61.c) Just as the Aṅgirases went to heaven by the path of the victorious ones.
{6} (18.2.1’) For Yama the Soma is purified; for Yama the oblation is prepared.
(18.2.1.c) To Yama goes the sacrifice, with Agni as its messenger, well-prepared. ||1||
Offer to Yama the most honey-sweet oblation and step forward!
This homage is for the seers, the first-born, the ancient makers of the path.
Offer to King Yama the ghee-rich milk as a sacrificial oblation.
(18.2.3.c) May he bestow upon us among the living a long life, that we may live on.
(18.2.4’) O Agni, do not burn him away, do not consume him with heat, do not scorch his skin or his body.
When you have made him cooked, O Jātavedas, then send him forth unto the Fathers.

When you have cooked him, O Jātavedas, then deliver him over to the Fathers. When he goes forth upon this path of the departed breath, then let him become one who obeys the will of the gods. He purifies himself through the three *trikadruka* vessels; six are the wide ones, and the Great One is indeed the single one.
(18.2.6.c) The Triṣṭubh and Gāyatrī meters—all these are established in Yama.
(18.2.7’) Go to the sun with your eye, to the wind with your breath; go to heaven and to earth according to your duties.
(18.2.7.c) Or go to the waters if that is where your welfare lies; take your stand among the plants with your bodily remains.
The unborn portion of thy heat—heat that with fervor; let thy flame burn it, let thy radiance consume it.
With those bodies of thine which are auspicious, O Jātavedas, convey him to the world of the righteous.
Those flames of thine, O Jātavedas, which are impetuous, and with which thou fillest the sky and the intermediate space—
(18.2.9.c) Let those [waters] follow the unaging one as he moves; then, with the most auspicious others, make him cooked.
9 (18.2.10’) Release him again, O Agni, to the fathers—he who, offered to you, wanders as one possessing his own portion (svadhā).
(18.2.10.c) Clothed in life, let him approach his remainder; let him be united with a body, full of luster. 10 {7}
Run past the two dogs, the offspring of Saramā, four-eyed and brindled, along the righteous path.
Then go to the gracious ancestors who rejoice in the banquet together with Yama.
O Yama, those two dogs of yours, the guardians, four-eyed, dwelling on the paths, who look upon men—
(18.2.12.c) O King, entrust him to those two; bestow upon him well-being and freedom from disease.

(18.2.13’) The two broad-nosed, honey-colored messengers of Yama, who delight in the life-force of men, wander among the people. May they restore to us today here the auspicious life-force, so that we may behold the sun. (18.2.13.c) May they grant us once more the blessed breath of life.

For some Soma flows clear; others sit beside the clarified butter; may he go even to those for whom the honey flows forth. Those who were of old at the winning of *ṛta*, born of *ṛta*, and increasers of *ṛta*.
O Yama, go also to the seers who practiced austerities, those born of austerity.
(18.2.15.c) To those who are invincible through austerity, who have gone to heaven by means of austerity, and who performed great austerities—to them indeed go also. (18.2.16)
Those heroes who fight in the great battles, those who sacrifice their own bodies for heaven,
or those who bestow thousands as sacrificial fees— may he go even to them.
Those seers with a thousand paths who protect the sun.
O Yama, may he go to the seers who practice austerity, those born of austerity. (18.2.18.c) Be pleasant to him, O Earth, thornless and providing a dwelling;
grant him wide-extending protection. (18.2.19)
(18.2.20) Be established in the unconfined, wide world of earth.
May those *svadhā* offerings which you performed while living be dripping with sweetness for you. (18.2.21) I summon your mind with my mind; come here, enjoying these houses.
(18.2.21.c) Unite with the Fathers, unite with Yama; may gentle, strengthening breezes blow upon you.
(18.2.22’) May the Maruts, the water-carriers, the swimmers of the flood, carry you upward;
making coolness by means of the goat, let them sprinkle you with rain—*bāl*. (18.2.22.c) 22.
I have called upon life for the sake of long life, for wisdom, for skill, and for living.
Let your spirit go to its own source; then hasten toward the ancestors.
Let not your mind [be lost] to the months, nor to your limbs, nor to your vital essence.

Whatever limb of yours has been cast away, whether it be the out-breath or the in-breath that has departed—let the Fathers, dwelling together in one nest, having gathered there, cause those limbs of yours to enter again from pasture to pasture.
The living have driven him away from his home; carry him out from here, beyond the village.
(18.2.27.c) Death was the messenger of Yama; the wise one caused the vital breaths to go to the fathers.

||27|| (18.2.28’) Those Dasyus who have entered among the fathers, who move about in the guise of kinsmen, consuming what is not offered—those who carry away *parāpuras* and *nipuras*, may Agni blow them away from this sacrifice. ||28||
May the Fathers enter here, making our home pleasant for us and extending our lifespan.
May we be able to approach them with oblations, living long through many autumns.
The cow which I give to you, and the milk-rice which [I give]—
(18.2.30.c) By him let there be no sustainer for the people—he who here was lifeless.
{9} (18.2.31’) Cross over to the one rich in horses, she who is most gracious, or toward Ṛkṣaka with a newer crossing.
(18.2.31.c) Let him who struck you be one deserving of death; let him not find any other portion.
Yama is the higher, Vivasvat the lower; beyond that I see nothing at all.
Upon Yama my sacrifice is established; Vivasvat has spread himself out after it.
They concealed the immortal one from mortals; having made her of similar appearance, they gave her to Vivasvat.
(18.2.33.c) And he brought the two Aśvins; that which was [there], Saraṇyū abandoned as a pair.
‖33‖ (18.2.34’) Those who are buried, those who are scattered, those who are burned, and those who are elevated—(18.2.34.c) O Agni, bring all those fathers here to eat the oblation. ‖34‖

(18.2.35) Those who have been consumed by fire and those who have not been consumed by fire, who rejoice in the midst of heaven through their own inherent power (*svadhā*),—you know them, O Jātavedas; may they enjoy the sacrifice and the sacrificial blade through their own inherent power.
(18.2.36) Be gracious with your heat; do not burn me excessively, O Agni; do not consume my body with your heat.
(18.2.36.c) Let your vigor be in the forests; let that which you sustain be upon the earth.
(18.2.37’) I grant this dwelling to him who has come here and has become mine.
Yama, the wise one, has declared this in reply: "Let him abide here by my riches. (18.2.37.c) 37.
(18.2.38) We measure out this measure so that it may not be exhausted for another hundred autumns. (18.2.39) We measure out this measure so that it may not be exhausted for another [period].

(18.2.39.c) Before a hundred autumns have passed for us. ||39|| (18.2.40’) We measure out this measure so that it may not fail us further. (18.2.40.c) Before a hundred autumns have passed for us. ||40|| {10}

(18.2.41) We measure out this measure so that it may not be exhausted for another hundred autumns before us. (18.2.42) We measure out this measure forth so that it may not be exhausted for another [period].
(18.2.42.c) Before a hundred autumns have passed for us.
||42|| (18.2.43’) We measure out this measure so that it may not be exhausted hereafter; (18.2.43.c) before a hundred autumns have passed for us. ||43||

(18.2.44’) Together we measure out this measure, so that it may not be exhausted for another hundred autumns before us. (18.2.45’) I have measured the measure; I have gone to the light of heaven; may I be long-lived.

(18.2.45.c) So that another month shall not come before a hundred autumns have passed. ||45|| Inhalation, exhalation, and the pervasive breath; life-force, sight for seeing the sun— By a path neither near nor far, go to the Fathers under the realm of Yama. ||46||

(18.2.47) Those who, being leaders and performing their labors, have passed away, leaving behind their enmities and being childless—having ascended to heaven, they have found the world, shining upon the back of the firmament.
(18.2.48) The lowest [world] is the watery sky; the middle one is the misty one.
The third is indeed the radiant sky, upon which the fathers sit. (48) Those who are our father’s fathers, those who are our grandfathers, who have entered the wide mid-air;
those who dwell upon the earth and in the heavens—to those fathers we pay homage with reverence. (49)
(18.2.50) This very thing, and nothing else, do you see as the sun in the sky;
O Earth, cover him with your soil, as a mother covers her son with the hem of her garment.
(18.2.51) This very thing, and nothing else, shall grow old; there is no other state beyond this.

(18.2.51.c) As a wife covers her husband with her garment, so do thou, O Earth, cover him. (18.2.52’) With the auspicious garment of Mother Earth I cover thee; that which is auspicious among the living is mine, and that which is *svadhā* among the fathers is thine. O Agni and Soma, you who prepare the way, bestow a pleasant dwelling and a treasure for the gods; create wide space.
Send forth Pūṣan, who carries [the offering]; go there by straight paths that lead the way.
May Pūṣan, the wise guardian of the world whose cattle are never lost, drive you forward from here.
(18.2.54.c) May Agni deliver you over to these fathers and to the gods who are easy to find.
(18.2.55’) May Āyus Viśvāyus protect you; may Pūṣan protect you on the distant path ahead.
(18.2.55.c) Where the doers of good deeds sit, where they have gone—there may the god Savitṛ place you.
(18.2.56’) “I yoke these two carriers for you, to carry you away to the world beyond.
By means of them, may you go down to the abode and the assembly of Yama.
(18.2.57’) “This garment has now first come to you; cast off that which you wore here before.”
(18.2.57.c) Pass on to that place your merit from sacrifices and charitable works, O wise one, where what was given by you among many kinsmen awaits you.

(18.2.58’) Envelop yourself with the protection of Agni using the cow-hides; cover yourself completely with fat and marrow, so that the bold one, exulting in his heat, may not seize you and consume you while he wanders about. (18.2.58.c) So that the grasping one, leaping up in his fury, may not burn you down.
Taking the staff from the hand of the one whose life has departed, together with his hearing, his luster, and his strength—
right here, may you remain, while we, possessing excellent heroes, conquer all insults and adversaries.
Taking the bow from the hand of the dead man, together with his dominion, his luster, and his strength.
(18.2.60.c) Gather up abundant and flourishing wealth; come hither toward the world of the living.

{12} (18.3.1’) This woman, choosing the world of her husband, has descended to you, O mortal, who have passed away. Upholding the ancient law (*dharma*), bestow upon her offspring and wealth in this world. {1}

(18.3.2) Rise up, O noble lady, toward the world of the living! Come to this one whose life has departed; he lies here as your bed. You have entered into this state of wifehood for your husband, who took your hand and desired you. (18.3.3) I beheld a young woman being led away—the living one being led around from among the dead.
(18.3.3.c) When she was shrouded by blinding darkness, I led her from the east toward the west.

(18.3.4’) O inviolable cow, conscious one, moving along the path of the gods toward the world of the living—this is your lord of cattle; welcome him, and cause him to ascend to the heavenly world. (18.3.4.c) 4.
(18.3.5) Near the sky, near the reed, you are the most helpful among the rivers;
O Agni, you are the bile of the waters.
(18.3.6) Whomever you have burned up, O Agni, quench him again.
(18.3.6.c) May the *kyāmbū* grow here, the *śāṇḍadūrvā*, and the *vyalkaśā*.
(18.3.7’) This is one [step] for you; before you is another. Enter into union with the third light.
At the time of entering, be beautiful in body and dear to the gods in the highest dwelling-place.
(18.3.8) Arise, go forth, run forward, and make your dwelling in the watery realm!
There, in harmony with the ancestors, rejoice with Soma and with the *svadhā* offerings.
(18.3.9) Move forward, gather your body together; let not your limbs be scattered, nor your frame be broken.
(18.3.9.c) Enter into that mind which has entered [the body]; go to that place where you take pleasure in the earth.

(18.3.10’) May the Soma-loving fathers and the gods anoint me with splendor, with honey, and with clarified butter. May they, furthering my sight, increase me so that I may reach old age and attain the full span of life. (13)
May Agni anoint me with splendor; may Viṣṇu anoint my wisdom in my mouth.
May all the gods bestow wealth upon me; may the pleasant waters purify me with their cleansing flows.
May Mitra and Varuṇa encompass me; may the Ādityas, the pillars of heaven, cause me to prosper.

(18.3.12.c) May Indra bestow luster upon my two hands; may Savitṛ grant me long life. ‖12‖ (18.3.13.a) He who was the first of mortals to die, he who was the first to depart for this world— (18.3.13.c) To Yama, the son of Vivasvat, the gatherer of men, to that king, pay honor with an oblation. ‖13‖
Depart, O Fathers, and come back again; this sacrifice of yours is anointed with honey.
Grant us here wealth and auspicious riches, and bestow upon us a fortune consisting of all heroic sons.
Kaṇva, Kakṣīvat, Purumīḍha, Agastya, Śyāvāśva, Sobhari, and Arcanānas.
(18.3.15.c) May this Viśvāmitra, Jamadagni, Atri, Kaśyapa, and Vāmadeva protect us.
||15|| (18.3.16’) O Viśvāmitra, Jamadagni, Vasiṣṭha, Bharadvāja, Gotama, and Vāmadeva!
(18.3.16.c) May Atri grant us strength through our salutations; O well-instructed fathers, be gracious to us. ||16||
Whose impurity do they pass over while being cleansed, bestowing upon us a newer and further span of life? May we, increasing in progeny and wealth, be fragrant within our homes.
They anoint themselves, they anoint themselves apart, they anoint themselves together; they lick their resolve and anoint it with honey.

(18.3.18.c) At the swelling of the river, the golden-purifying ones seize the bull as he falls, the sacrificial animal, within these [waters]. 18 (18.3.19.a) O Fathers, with that which is your joy and that which is yours belonging to Soma, be united with us; for you have become self-glorious.
(18.3.19.c) Listen well, O swift-moving sages, when you are invoked at the sacrifice, you who are easy to find. 19
The Atris, the Angirases, the Navagvas, who were seekers of the sacrifice, bestowers of gifts, and maintainers of the ritual;
you who are givers of sacrificial fees and doers of good deeds—rejoice here upon this sacred grass.
And so, O Agni, as our ancient fathers of old, aspiring toward the *ṛta*, [attained their goal]...
(18.3.21.c) Moving toward the pure ones, they meditated, chanting their hymns; cleaving the earth, they disclosed the ruddy cows.

||21|| (18.3.22’) Performing good deeds, radiant, seeking the gods, like smiths smelting ore, the gods forged their births. (18.3.22.c) Kindling Agni and strengthening Indra, they have prepared for us a vast assembly rich in cattle. ||22||
Like a powerful man looking upon herds of cattle in a rich pasture, he has beheld the final generations of the gods.

Even mortals have yearned for the *urvaśīs*; the noble one has brought prosperity even to the lowliest man. We have worked for you with skillful hands; we have become [your servants], as the radiant dawns have dawned according to the cosmic order (*ṛta*).
(18.3.24.c) All that which the gods protect is auspicious; may we, blessed with brave sons, speak aloud at the assembly.
(18.3.25’) May Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, protect me from the eastern quarter, as the earth, shaken by his arms, protects the heavens above.
We sacrifice to the makers of worlds and the makers of paths, you who are here present as the recipients of the oblations among the gods.
May Dhātṛ protect me from the southern quarter against Nirṛti; may the earth, shaken by his arms, be as above as heaven.
We worship the world-makers and the path-makers who are here, you who are the recipients of the oblations among the gods.
May Aditi, together with the Ādityas, protect me from the western quarter against Nirṛti; may the earth, shaken by her arms, be as above as heaven.
(18.3.27.c) We worship those who created the worlds, who made the paths, you who are here as the recipients of the oblations among the gods.
(27) (18.3.28’) May Soma, together with all the gods, protect me from the northern quarter; may the earth, shaken by his arms, shield me as the sky protects from above.
(18.3.28.c) We worship those who created the worlds, who made the paths, you who are here as the recipients of the oblations among the gods. (28)
May the supporter, the sustainer, hold you up, as Savitṛ holds the light aloft above the sky.
We worship those world-makers and path-makers who are here present as the recipients of the oblations among the gods.
(18.3.29) In the eastern quarter, before it is closed in, I place you within the *svadhā* offering, like the earth moved by the arms [of the gods] above the sky. (18.3.30)

(18.3.30.c) We worship those who created the worlds and made the paths, you who are here as the recipients of the oblations among the gods. {15} (18.3.31’) In the southern quarter, before it was closed, I place you within the *svadhā* offering, like the earth moved by the arms [of Indra] above the sky.
(18.3.31.c) We worship those who created the worlds and made the paths, you who are here as the recipients of the oblations among the gods. {16}
In the western quarter, before it is closed, I place you within the *svadhā* offering, as the earth, moved by the arms [of the gods], is above the sky.
We worship those world-makers and path-makers who are here present as the recipients of the oblations among the gods.
In the northern quarter, before it is closed, I place you within the *svadhā* offering, as the earth, moved by the arms [of the gods], is above the sky.
(18.3.33.c) We worship those who created the worlds and made the paths, you who are here as the recipients of the oblations among the gods.
(18.3.34’) In the firm quarter, before the world was encompassed, I place you within the *svadhā* offering, like the earth supported by arms above the sky.
(18.3.34.c) We worship those who created the worlds and made the paths, you who are here as the recipients of the oblations among the gods.
(18.3.35) In the upward direction, before [the end], I place you within the *svadhā* offering, as one moved by the arms, like the earth above the sky.
We worship the world-makers and path-makers who are here, you who are the sharers of the oblation among the gods.
(18.3.36) You are the supporter; you are the sustainer; you are the bull.
(18.3.37) You are full of water, you are full of honey, you are full of wind.

(18.3.38) From here and from there may they protect me, as you two came striving together like twins. Men, seeking the gods, brought you forward; sit down, you who know your own place. (18.3.38c) May they sit down, knowing their own place.
Be well-seated for our Soma; we yoke you both with ancient prayer and salutations.
The hymn goes forth like a wise man upon his path; may all the immortals hear this.
He has ascended the three steps of the radiant one; he has followed this four-footed [path] according to the sacred law.
(18.3.40.c) With the syllable he measures out the hymn; at the navel of Cosmic Order he purifies it thoroughly.
{16} (18.3.41’) For the sake of the gods he chose death; for the sake of progeny, did he not choose immortality?
Bṛhaspati, the seer, stretched out the sacrifice; Yama cast off his beloved body. {41}
O Agni Jātavedas, you who have been praised, having made the offerings fragrant, you have conveyed them;
you have given them to the Fathers, and they have eaten them with the *svadhā* call. Eat, O God, these presented oblations!
(42) Seated in the lap of the ruddy dawns, bestow wealth upon the mortal who offers gifts. (43)
(18.3.43.c) O fathers, bestow that wealth upon your sons; grant them strength here.

(18.3.44’) O Agniṣvātta fathers, come hither; sit each in his proper seat, O excellent leaders. Having eaten the oblations presented upon the sacrificial grass, grant us wealth consisting of all heroic sons.
The Soma-loving fathers have been summoned to our dear offerings upon the sacrificial grass. May they come; may they hear us here; may they speak for us; may they protect us.
(45) Those who are the fathers of our father, those grandfathers, the most excellent ones, who have followed after the drinking of the Soma—(46)

(18.3.46.c) May Yama, rejoicing with them, desiring the oblations, eat them according to his desire along with those who desire them.
