(18.3.48) O Agni, come hither on the same chariot with Indra and the swift gods—those who are true, eaters of the oblation, and drinkers of the oblation—with the ancient seers of noble wisdom who sit by the *gharma* vessel.
(18.3.49) Approach this mother, the earth; approach the wide-extending, most gracious Pṛthivī.
(18.3.49.c) Soft as wool is the earth for those who possess sacrificial gifts; may she protect you from the front on the distant path.
(18.3.50’) Open wide, O Earth; do not press down upon him. Be easy of access to him, easy of approach. As a mother covers her son with the hem of her garment, so do you, O Earth, cover him. (50) {17}
May the earth, swelling wide, stand firm; may a thousand columns rise up to support it.
May those dwellings drip with clarified butter, and may they be pleasant and a refuge for him here at all times.
(51) I prop up the earth around you; as I set down this clod of earth, may I suffer no harm. (52)

(18.3.52.c) The Fathers uphold this pillar; may Yama prepare for you a dwelling there. (18.3.53’) O Agni, do not overturn this cup, which is dear to the gods and to those worthy of Soma. This is the cup from which the gods drink; in it, let the immortal gods rejoice. (18.3.53.c) In that cup from which the gods drink, let the immortal gods rejoice. Atharvan brought a full cup for Indra, the possessor of strength;
in it he prepares the draught of good deeds; therein Indu flows at all times.
Whatever the black bird has pecked at you, or the ant, the serpent, or even the wild beast—[may it be removed].
(18.3.55.c) May Agni and Soma—who has entered into the Brahmins—make that entirely free from disease.
||55|| (18.3.56’) The plants are full of milk; full of milk is my own milk.
(18.3.56.c) That which is the milk of the milk of the waters—with that, may he purify me together. ||56||
(18.3.57) Let these women, not widows and having good husbands, touch [him] with collyrium and clarified butter.
Free from tears, free from disease, and possessing fine jewels, let the wives ascend first to the place of origin.
(18.3.58) Unite with the Fathers, unite with Yama, and with the merit of your sacrifices and pious works in the highest heaven.
(18.3.58.c) Having left behind what is blameworthy, go once more to your setting; gather together with a body full of splendor!

(18.3.59’) Those who are the fathers of our father, those who are our grandfathers, who have entered the wide mid-air— from them may Asunīti today, by her own will, fashion our bodies according to our desire. (18.3.59.c)
May the mist be auspicious for you; may the spray of water cool you. O cool one, O possessor of coolness! O refreshing one, O possessor of refreshment!
O female frog, be auspicious in the waters; pacify this fire of ours. 60. {18}
May Vivasvān grant us fearlessness—he who is the good protector, the quick-giver, the bounteous giver.
May these many heroes be ours here; may prosperity consisting of cattle and horses be mine.
(61) May Vivasvān establish us in immortality; let death pass away and immortality come to us. (62)

(18.3.62.c) May he protect these men until old age; let not their life-breaths go to Yama. (18.3.63’) He who, like the vastness of the mid-air, has established himself as the sage of the fathers and the guardian of thoughts—worship him with oblations, O you who have all Mitra as friend; may that Yama grant us further life. (18.3.64) Ascend to the highest heaven, O seers; do not be afraid.
O drinkers of Soma, you who drink the Soma, this oblation is prepared for you; we have gone to the highest light.
(18.3.65) With his great banner Agni shines forth; like a bull, he bellows unto the two worlds.
(18.3.65.c) Even from the very limit of heaven he has brought [light] near; the buffalo has grown great in the lap of the waters.

(18.3.66’) When they beheld thee with longing in their hearts as thou wert flying toward the firmament like a well-winged bird—(18.3.66.c) thee, the golden-winged messenger of Varuṇa, the restless bird in the womb of Yama.
O Indra, bring us wisdom, just as a father provides for his sons. Teach us, O much-invoked one, on this path; living, may we attain the light.
[67] The jars which the gods held for you, covered with cakes—
(18.3.68.c) May they be yours—self-sustaining, honeyed, and dripping with ghee.

||68|| (18.3.69’) Those parched grains mixed with sesame seeds which I scatter for you, self-sustaining; (18.3.69.c) may they be yours—pervasive and powerful; may King Yama grant his approval of them for you. ||69||
Give back again, O Lord of the Forest, that which has been placed within you, so that he may sit in the abode of Yama, speaking the sacred ordinances.
Grasp it, O Jātavedas; let your splendor be radiant.
(18.3.71.c) Burn his body; place him in the world of those who have performed good deeds.
(18.3.72’) Those ancestors of yours who have passed away before, and those who came later—to them let this stream of clarified butter go, flowing with a hundred streams.
(18.3.73’) Ascend this, shaking off your impurities; here your own [lights] shine forth loftily.
(18.3.73.c) Go forward; do not leave us from the midst, you who are the first among the fathers in this world.
{19} (18.4.1’) Ascend the mother, O Jātavedas; with the paths of the fathers, I cause you all to ascend together.
(18.4.1.c) Sent forth with the oblations, O bearer of oblations, carry the sacrificer; joined together, place him in the world of the righteous.
(18.4.2’) The gods and the seasons prepare the sacrifice: the oblation, the sacrificial cake, the ladles, and the implements of sacrifice.
(18.4.2.c) Go by those paths traveled by the gods, by which those who have sacrificed go to the heavenly world.
Behold well the path of Truth, along which the Angirases, the doers of good deeds, travel.
Go by those paths to heaven, where the Ādityas consume the honey; settle yourself upon the third firmament.
Three birds with beautiful wings, the offspring of the lower [world], are perched upon the ridge of the firmament, on its highest surface.
(18.4.4.c) May the heavenly worlds, established with immortality, yield nourishment and vigor for the sacrificer.
(18.4.5’) The *juhū* has supported the sky, the *upabhṛt* the intermediate space, and the *dhruvā* has supported the earth as the foundation.
(18.4.5.c) May these worlds, the heavenly ones with ghee upon their backs, yield every desire for the sacrificer.

(18.4.6) Ascend, O *dhruvā* ladle, upon the earth that nourishes all; stride forth to the intermediate space with the *upabhṛt*. Go to the sky with the *juhū*, together with the sacrificer; with the *sruva* as your calf, milk all the swelling quarters, remaining free from anger. (18.4.7) By means of the fords they cross the steep descents and the great [waters], by which the performers of sacrifice, the doers of good deeds, go.

(18.4.7.c) Here they have established a world for the sacrificer, as the quarters and the beings were fashioned. (18.4.8’) The first fire is the path of the Aṅgirases; the Gārhapatya fire is the path of the Ādityas; the Dakṣiṇāgni fire is the path of the sacrificial gifts. With all your limbs intact, come hither, full of strength, to the majesty of Agni as ordained by the Brahman. (18.4.9) May the eastern fire warm you; may it grant peace from the front. May the Gārhapatya fire warm you from behind; may it grant peace. (18.4.9c) May the Dakṣiṇāgni fire warm you; may it grant protection and armor. From the north, from the center, from the intermediate space, and from every direction, O Agni, protect us from the terrible.
9 (18.4.10) O Agnis, with your most auspicious bodies, [lead] the sacrificer to the heavenly world.
(18.4.10.c) Having become horses, carry us on your backs where they rejoice in communal revelry with the gods. 10.
(18.4.11’) O Agni, burn him gently from behind, gently from the front; burn him gently from above and gently from below.
(18.4.11.c) O Jātavedas, you who are one yet divided threefold, place him properly in the world of the righteous. 11.
(18.4.12’) May the fires, well-kindled, take hold of the sacrificial portion belonging to Prajāpati, O Jātavedas;
making it cooked, do not cast it away from here.
(18.4.13’) The sacrifice goes forth, spread out and being prepared, toward the sacrificer’s world in heaven.
(18.4.13.c) May the fires accept him, who is offered as a whole oblation, as the holy one belonging to Prajāpati, O Jātavedas.
(18.4.14’) Having sacrificed, he has ascended the piled fire, intending to fly up from the back of the firmament to heaven.
For him, the luminous, heavenly path leading to the gods shines forth through the sky for his well-performed deed. (18.4.14.c) 14.
Agni is your Hotṛ, Bṛhaspati is your Adhvaryu; may Indra be your Brahman priest on the right.
This sacrifice, offered and completed, goes to where the former path of the offerings lies.
May the oblation of rice-porridge, accompanied by cakes and milk, settle here.
(18.4.16.c) We worship those who made the worlds, those who made the paths, you who are here as the recipients of the oblations among the gods.
||16|| (18.4.17’) May the sacrificial porridge, accompanied by cakes and curds, settle here.
(18.4.17.c) We worship those who made the worlds, those who made the paths, you who are here as the recipients of the oblations among the gods. ||17||
May the sacrificial porridge, rich in cakes and rich in drops, settle here.
We worship those world-makers and path-makers who are present here as the recipients of the oblations of the gods.
May the sacrificial porridge, rich in cakes and rich in ghee, settle here.

(18.4.19.c) We worship those who made the worlds, who made the paths, who here are the recipients of the oblations among the gods. (18.4.20’) May the sacrificial porridge, rich in cakes and rich in meat, sit here.
We worship those who made the worlds, who made the paths, who here are the recipients of the oblations among the gods. (21)
May the sacrificial porridge, rich in cakes and rich in food, sit here.
We worship those world-makers and path-makers who are present here as the recipients of the oblations of the gods. May the sacrificial porridge, rich in cakes and rich in honey, sit here.

(18.4.22.c) We worship the makers of the world, the makers of paths, you who are here as the recipients of the oblations among the gods. ||22|| (18.4.23’) May the sacrificial porridge, rich in cakes and rich in juices, settle here.
(18.4.23.c) We worship the makers of the world, the makers of paths, you who are here as the recipients of the oblations among the gods. ||23||
May the sacrificial porridge, accompanied by cakes and free from defects, settle here.

We worship those world-makers and path-makers who are present here as the recipients of the oblations among the gods. Those jars which the gods supported for you, covered with cakes—[may they be ours].
(18.4.25.c) May these offerings be yours—self-sustaining, honeyed, and dripping with ghee.

||25|| (18.4.26’) These parched grains mixed with sesame seeds, which I scatter for you as self-sustaining oblations— (18.4.26.c) may they be powerful and abundant for you; may King Yama grant his approval of them for you. ||26||
(18.4.27’) Abundant imperishability.
(27) (18.4.28’) The drop has fallen upon the earth, after heaven, upon this womb and that which was before;
following the drop as it moves along toward the common womb, I offer it according to the seven priestly offices. (28)
They who behold with human eyes the wind that has a hundred streams, the sun that finds the light—heirs of wealth;
they who satisfy and ever bestow, they milk the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*) whose mother is the sevenfold one.
They milk the vessel, the four-holed beaker, the nourishing cow (*iḍā*), the honey-sweet one, for well-being.
(18.4.30.c) O Agni, do not harm the strengthening, exhilarating Aditi among the people in the highest heaven.
{22} (18.4.31’) This garment the god Savitṛ gives to you for wearing;
wearing that silken robe in the realm of King Yama, proceed. (18.4.31.c) 31.
The parched grain became a cow; sesame was her calf.
Indeed, one lives upon that inexhaustible [cow] in the kingdom of King Yama.
May these cows of yours be givers of all desires.

(18.4.33.c) Let the brindled ones, the falcon-colored ones, those of uniform appearance and those of diverse forms, with sesame-seed calves, attend upon you here. (18.4.34’) These are his: the brindled parched grains, the tawny, the falcon-colored, the black parched grains, and the ruddy milch-cows; may they, with sesame-seed calves, yielding nourishment for him, be ever-present and never-failing. In Vaiśvānara I offer this oblation, a thousandfold fountain with a hundred streams. Swelling, it sustains the father, the grandfather, and the great-grandfather.
A thousandfold, a hundred-streamed, inexhaustible fountain, spreading wide upon the surface of the waters.

Right here be a winner of wealth; right here be your thought, right here your resolve. Right here be more heroic, a bestower of vitality, unassailed.
O waters, sweet with honey, satisfying sons and grandsons—(38–39)
(18.4.39.c) May the divine Waters, milking out the *svadhā* offering and immortality for the Fathers, satisfy both [the living and the dead].
39. (18.4.40’) O Waters, send forth Agni toward the Fathers; may my Fathers enjoy this sacrifice.
(18.4.40.c) Those who attend upon the strength of her who sits [within], may they bestow upon us wealth consisting of all heroic sons. 40. {23}
They kindle the immortal one, the bearer of oblations who loves clarified butter;
he knows the hidden treasures and the ancestors who have gone to the far distance.
Whatever stirred mash, whatever cooked rice, and whatever meat I offer to you—
(18.4.42.c) May they be yours—possessing the *svadhā* offering, honeyed, and dripping with clarified butter.

||42|| (18.4.43’) Those parched grains (*dhānā*) mixed with sesame seeds, accompanied by the *svadhā* offering, which I scatter for you— (18.4.43.c) may they be yours, productive and abundant; may King Yama grant his approval for them. ||43||
This is the path, the former and the later, by which your ancestors have departed. Those who go before you, the leaders and followers of this way—they carry you to the world of the righteous.
(18.4.44) Those seeking the gods invoke Sarasvatī; they invoke Sarasvatī while the sacrifice is being performed. (18.4.45)
(18.4.45.c) The doers of good deeds invoke Sarasvatī; may Sarasvatī grant what is desirable to the donor.

(18.4.46’) The fathers invoke Sarasvatī as they approach the sacrifice from the south; having sat down upon this sacred grass (*barhis*), rejoice! Bestow upon us food free from disease. (18.4.46.c) 46.

O Sarasvatī, you who have come on the same chariot with the hymns, O Goddess, rejoicing with the *svadhā* offerings along with the Fathers—here, bestow upon the sacrificer a portion of the *iḍā* worth a thousandfold, and the increase of wealth.
I cause you, the Earth, to enter the earth; may the divine Dhātṛ extend our lifespan.
(18.4.48.c) May he who finds wealth come to you from afar; then, having died, may they be united with the ancestors.
(48) (18.4.49’) Come forth together! Wipe away that which others have spoken against you here.
(18.4.49.c) O inviolable ones, this [gift] is more desirable than that of the giver; it is for me, to be enjoyed here among the ancestors. (49)
(18.4.50) This auspicious sacrificial fee has come from the south; it was given by him as one that is well-milking and bestowing vigor.
May she, while clinging to the living in their youth, deliver these [ancestors] over to old age.
(18.4.51) I bring forth this sacred grass for the ancestors; I spread it out higher for the living gods.
(18.4.51.c) Ascend that, O man, becoming fit for sacrifice; may the fathers recognize you as you depart.
(18.4.52’) Sit upon this sacred grass; you have become fit for sacrifice; may the fathers recognize you as you depart.
(18.4.52.c) Assemble your body limb by limb; I restore your members with a sacred prayer.
May Parṇa, the king, the covering of the sacrificial vessels, come to us with vigor, strength, endurance, and vital power;
bestowing life upon those who live, for the sake of long-lived existence through a hundred autumns.
May he, the portion of vigor who begot this [world], attain lordship over the stones and foods.
(18.4.54.c) Worship him with oblations, O Viśvāmitras; may he, Yama, grant us further life.
(18.4.55’) Just as the five men built a mansion for Yama, so do I build this mansion, that many may belong to me. (18.4.55.c) So do I build this mansion, that many may belong to me.
"Take up this gold which your father bore in former times;
cleanse the right hand of your father as he goes to heaven.
"And those who are living, and those who are dead, those who are born, and those who are worthy of sacrifice..."
(18.4.57.c) Let a stream of clarified butter flow for them, an overflowing torrent of honey.
(18.4.58’) The bull of hymns, the far-seeing one, flows clear; the sun of days, the furtherer of dawns from heaven.
The breath of the rivers has bellowed toward the jars, entering the heart of Indra with inspired thought. (18.4.58.c) He has entered the heart of Indra with inspired thought.
(18.4.59) May your brilliant smoke envelop the sky; may your bright [flame] spread forth as peace. For like the sun with its radiance, you, O Purifier, shine with your form.
(18.4.60) The Soma-drop goes forward to the appointed place of Indra; as a friend, he does not violate the agreements of his friend.
Like a youth toward maidens, Soma flows together into the jar by a path of a hundred courses.
They have eaten and they have rejoiced; they have shaken off their dear [impurities].
The self-luminous sages, the most youthful, have offered praise; we entreat them.
Come, O Soma-loving fathers, by the deep paths traveled by the ancestors.
Bestowing upon us long life and progeny, favor us with the increase of wealth.
Depart, O Soma-loving fathers, by the deep paths of antiquity.
(18.4.63.c) Then, after a month, come back again to our homes, to eat the oblation, possessing good offspring and brave sons.

(18.4.64’) That one limb of yours which Agni Jātavedas abandoned when sending you to the world of the fathers— (18.4.64.c) that I now replenish for you once more; O Fathers, being whole-limbed, rejoice in heaven.
Jātavedas has been sent as a messenger; at evening, at the close of day, he is to be praised by men.
You have given [the offerings] to the ancestors; they have eaten them with the *svadhā* call. Eat, O God, these presented oblations.
O you there, here is your mind, as kinsmen [gaze upon] the hump of a bull.
(18.4.66.c) Cover him with the earth.
(18.4.67’) May the worlds, the seats of the fathers, be made beautiful; I seat you in the world that is the seat of the fathers.
(18.4.68’) You are the sacrificial grass for those who are our fathers.
(18.4.69) O Varuṇa, loosen the uppermost bond from us; cast down the lowest.
Then, O Āditya, being under your protection, may we be sinless before Aditi.
(18.4.70) O Varuṇa, release from us all those bonds with which one is bound at the elbow and those with which one is bound at the forearm.
(18.4.70.c) Then may we live for a hundred autumns, O King, protected and guarded by you.
70 (18.4.71’) To Agni Kavyavāhana, svadhā! Homage! 71 (18.4.72’) To Soma Pitṛmat, svadhā! Homage! 72

(18.4.73) Svadhā! Adoration to the ancestors accompanied by Soma! (73) (18.4.74) Svadhā! Adoration to Yama, who possesses the ancestors! (74) (18.4.75) This, O great-grandfather, is for you, svadhā; and for those who follow you. (75)
(18.4.76) This [is] for you, O grandfather, svadhā, and for those who follow you. (18.4.77) This [is] for you, O father, svadhā. (18.4.78) Svadhā to the fathers who dwell upon the earth.
(18.4.79) Svadhā to the fathers who dwell in the intermediate space!
(18.4.80) Svadhā to the fathers who dwell in heaven!
(18.4.81) Homage to you, O fathers, for strength; homage to you, O fathers, for sap!
Homage to you, O fathers, for your brilliance; homage to you, O fathers, for your wrath.
(82) Homage to you, O fathers, for that which is terrible; homage to you, O fathers, for that which is cruel.
(83) Homage to you, O fathers, for that which is auspicious; homage to you, O fathers, for that which is pleasant. (84)
Homage to you, O fathers; the *svadhā* offering is for you, O fathers.
(85) Those who are here, O fathers—those fathers who are here—you are they, and they are yours. May you become the most excellent among them.
(86) Those who are living fathers here—we are they here. (87)
(18.4.87.c) May we follow after you; may we be the best among them.
(18.4.88’) O Agni, let us kindle you, the radiant, the undecaying god, so that this most glorious fuel of yours may shine in the sky.
(18.4.88.e) Bring nourishment to those who praise you!

‖88‖ (18.4.89’) The moon moves within the waters; the fair-winged bird flies in the sky. O ye lightnings with golden rims, they find not your place; O Heaven and Earth, take note of this for me! ‖89‖ {28}
(19.1.1) Let the rivers flow together; let the winds and the winged birds come together.
May the songs increase this sacrifice; I offer it with the oblation that flows together.
(19.1.2) O offerings, protect this sacrifice; O outpourings, likewise protect this sacrifice. May the songs increase this sacrifice; I offer it with the oblation that flows together.
(19.1.3’) Grasping him by every form and every age, I embrace him.
May the four quarters increase this sacrifice; I offer it with the flowing oblation.
(19.2.1’) May the waters from the Himalayas be auspicious for you, and may the waters from the springs be auspicious for you.
(19.2.1.c) May the flowing waters be auspicious for you, and may the rains be auspicious for you.
‖1‖ (19.2.2’) May the waters of the desert be auspicious for you, and may those of the marshes be auspicious for you.
(19.2.2.c) May the waters from dug wells be auspicious for you, and those brought in jars be auspicious. ‖2‖
(19.2.3) The cloudless ones, digging, the inspired singers, the workers in the depths—
(19.2.3c) we speak toward the waters, the physicians more skilled than physicians.
(19.2.4) Of the celestial waters, of the flowing waters...
(19.2.4.c) At the washing of the waters, you become swift horses.
(19.2.5’) Those waters are auspicious, those waters are healers that remove disease;
just as they provide refreshment and joy, so do you grant them healing medicines.
From heaven, from earth, from the intermediate space, from the trees, and from the plants—from wherever you, Jātavedas, are distributed, come to us here, praised and well-pleased.
Whatever majesty of yours is in the waters, whatever is in the forests, whatever is in the plants, in the cattle, and within the waters; [from all that, come to us].

(19.3.2.c) O Agni, gather together all your bodies; with them come to us, you who are the eternal giver of wealth. (19.3.3’) That majesty of yours which is heavenly among the gods, that body of yours which has entered into the fathers, and that prosperity of yours which has spread among men—O Agni, bestow upon us wealth through those very powers.
To the one with attentive ears, the seer who is to be known, I approach with words and hymns for the sake of a gift.
May that from which there is fear become for us freedom from fear; O Agni, sacrifice to appease the wrath of the gods.
The oblation which Atharvan offered first, which Jātavedas, once born, made into a sacrificial gift—

(19.4.1.c) This very [prayer] I invoke for you as the first; may Agni, satisfied by these, carry the oblation. To Agni, Svāhā! (19.4.2’) I place before me the goddess Ākūti, the fortunate one; may she, the mother of thought, be easy for us to invoke. Whatever hope I pursue, may that be mine alone; may I find her entered into my mind.
O Bṛhaspati, come to us with our intention; come to us with our intention. Furthermore, bestow upon us fortune, and furthermore, be easy for us to invoke.
May Bṛhaspati, the descendant of Aṅgiras, acknowledge my intention and this speech.
(19.4.4.c) May that Kāma, after whom the gods have become the deities, follow us as our excellent guide.
(19.5.1’) Indra is the king of the moving world and of the peoples, over all that exists in manifold forms upon the earth.
From there he bestows riches upon the donor; may he, being praised, impel his bounty hither toward us.
The Person has a thousand arms, a thousand eyes, and a thousand feet;
having encompassed the earth on every side, he stood ten fingers' breadth beyond it.
With three steps he ascended to heaven, while one foot of his remained here once more.
Thus he strode out in all directions across both the eating and the non-eating.
2. So great is his majesty, and yet the Puruṣa is even greater than that.
All beings constitute one quarter of him; his three quarters are the immortal in heaven. 3.
(19.6.4) This entire world is indeed the Puruṣa—whatever has been and whatever is to be;
moreover, he is the lord of immortality, that which came into being together with what is other than himself.
(19.6.5) When they divided the Puruṣa, into how many parts did they apportion him?
(19.6.5.c) What was his mouth? What were his arms? What are his thighs and feet called?
(19.6.6’) The Brāhmaṇa was his mouth; his arms became the Rājanya;
that which was his waist became the Vaiśya; from his feet the Śūdra was born.
The moon was born from his mind; from his eye the sun was born;
from his mouth Indra and Agni were born; from his breath Vāyu was born. From his navel the intermediate space arose; from his head the sky evolved.
(19.6.8.c) From his feet the earth was formed, and from his hearing the directions; thus they fashioned the worlds.
(19.6.9’) In the beginning, Virāj came into being; from Virāj arose Puruṣa.
Once born, he extended beyond the earth—both behind and before. (19.6.9.c) 9.
When the gods performed the sacrifice with man as the oblation,
spring was its clarified butter, summer the fuel, and autumn the offering.
They sprinkled that sacrifice— the Puruṣa born in the beginning— with the rainy season.
By him the gods sacrificed—the Sādhyas and the Vasus.
From him were born horses, and whatever animals have two rows of teeth;
from him indeed cows were born, and from him goats and sheep were produced.
From that sacrifice in which everything was offered, the Ṛg-verses and the Sāman-chants were born;
from it the meters were born, and from it the Yajus-formulas were produced.
From that sacrifice in which everything was offered, the speckled butter was gathered.
He made those animals belonging to Vāyu—those which are wild and those which are domestic.
(19.6.14.c) Seven were the enclosing sticks for his mouth; thrice seven were the fuel-sticks prepared.
(19.6.15.c) When the gods, performing the sacrifice, bound Puruṣa as the victim. (19.6.15)

From the head of the great god, seventy-seven rays were born from King Soma, once he had been produced from Puruṣa. The variegated lights in heaven, the crawling things in the world, and the swift-moving beings were all produced together.
(19.7.1.c) Desiring Turmiśa’s favor, I honor the days and the firmament with my songs.
(19.7.2’) O Agni, may Kṛttikā and Rohiṇī be easy to invoke; may Mṛgaśiras be auspicious and Ārdrā bring peace.
(19.7.2.c) May the two Punarvasūs, Sūnṛtā, Puṣya, Bhānu, Āśleṣā, and Maghā be my path.
May Puṣya, Pūrvaphalgunī, and here Hasta, Citrā, Śivā, and Svāti be auspicious and bring me happiness.
May Rādhā, Viśākhā, the easily invoked Anurādhā, Jyeṣṭhā, the excellent Nakṣatra, and Mūla be free from harm.
May Pūrvāṣāḍhā grant me food, and may the divine Uttarāṣāḍhā bring me strength.

(19.7.4.c) May Abhijit grant me merit; may Śravaṇa and Śraviṣṭhā bring about well-being. (19.7.5’) May the great Śatabhiṣaj grant me wide space; may the two Proṣṭhapadas grant me good protection. (19.7.5.c) May Revatī and the two Aśvayujas bring me fortune; may the Bharaṇīs bring me wealth.

Whatever constellations are in heaven, in the intermediate space, in the waters, on the earth, or upon the mountains, and those in all directions— which the moon traverses as it courses through them— may they all be auspicious for me.
May these twenty-eight auspicious and powerful ones grant me their favorable conjunction.
(19.8.2.c) I resort to yoga and to security; I resort to security and to yoga. Let there be homage to day and night!

||2|| (19.8.3’) May there be well-being for me: a good morning, a good evening, a good day, a good deer, and a good omen for me. O Agni, may my invocation be successful; having gone to the immortal state for well-being, may I return again in joy. ||3||
(19.8.4) The sighing, the sneezing, the reproach, the snorting—drive all these away from me with empty jars, O Savitṛ!
(19.8.5) May we avoid evil sneezing; may we enjoy auspicious sneezing.
(19.8.5.c) O Evil One, may the jackal urinate upon your nose, and may the one who goes to merit [urinate] upon you!
(19.8.6’) O Brahmaṇaspati, those winds which blow in all directions—O Indra, making them flow together, make them most auspicious for me!
(19.8.6.c) O Indra, making them flow together, make them most auspicious for me!
May there be well-being for us; may there be fearlessness for us; homage be to day and night!
Peaceful be the sky, peaceful the earth, and peaceful this vast mid-air.
Peaceful be the waters rich with moisture; may the plants be peaceful for us.
(19.9.2) May the preceding omens be pacified; may all that we have done and left undone be peaceful for us. May the past and the future be peaceful; may everything indeed be peace for us.
(19.9.3) This goddess of speech, Parameṣṭhinī, who is sharpened by the Brahman—
(19.9.3.c) By that very [power] with which he created the terrible, by that same [power] may there be peace for us.
(19.9.4’) This mind of Parameṣṭhin, or your speech, sharpened by sacred knowledge—by that very [power] with which he created the terrible, by that same [power] may there be peace for us.
(19.9.4.c) By that very [power] with which he created the terrible, by that same [power] may there be peace for us.

(19.9.5) These five sense-faculties, with the mind as the sixth, which have been sharpened within my heart by Brahmā— by those very [faculties] through which he created the terrible, may there be peace for us. (19.9.6) May Mitra be auspicious to us, may Varuṇa be auspicious, may Viṣṇu be auspicious, and may Prajāpati be auspicious.
May Indra and Bṛhaspati be auspicious to us; may Aryaman be auspicious to us.
(7) May Mitra be auspicious to us, Varuṇa be auspicious, Vivasvat be auspicious, and Antaka be auspicious.
May terrestrial and atmospheric portents be auspicious to us, and the planets that move in heaven be auspicious to us. (8)
May the trembling earth be auspicious to us; may the meteor that has been struck down be auspicious.
May cows with red milk be auspicious, and may the earth as it flows downward be auspicious.
(8) May a constellation struck by a meteor be auspicious to us; may sorceries be auspicious to us, and may magical spells be auspicious. (9)
May the buried pits and the firebrands be auspicious to us; may the portents of the land likewise be auspicious to us.
(9) May the lunar planets be auspicious to us, and may the sun together with Rāhu be auspicious.
May Death and the comet Dhūmaketu be auspicious to us, and may the Rudras of piercing splendor be auspicious. (10)
May the Rudras be auspicious, may the Vasus be auspicious, may the Ādityas be auspicious, and may the Agnis be auspicious.
May the great seers and gods be auspicious to us; may the gods be auspicious, and may Bṛhaspati be auspicious.
(11) May Brahmā, Prajāpati, Dhātṛ, the worlds, the Vedas, the seven seers, and the fires [be auspicious]. (12)
(19.9.12.c) By them has my auspicious rite been performed; may Indra grant me protection, may the Brahman grant me protection.
(19.9.12.e) May all the gods grant me protection; may every god grant me protection.
12 (19.9.13’) Whatever peaceful things the Seven Seers know in this world, [may they be mine].
(19.9.13.c) May all things be auspicious for me; may there be auspiciousness for me, may there be fearlessness for me.

‖13‖ (19.9.14’) Earth is peace, the intermediate space is peace, heaven is peace, the waters are peace, the herbs are peace, the trees are peace, all the gods are peace for me, all the gods are peace for me—peace, peace, peace with [all] peaces.

(19.9.14.c) Whatever here is terrible, whatever here is cruel, whatever here is evil—may that all be stilled, may that be auspicious; may there be peace for us in every way. ‖14‖ (19.10.1’) May Indra and Agni be gracious to us with their protections; may Indra and Varuṇa, to whom oblations are offered, be gracious to us. (19.10.1.c) May Indra and Soma be gracious for our well-being and for health; may Indra and Pūṣan be gracious to us in the winning of booty. ‖1‖
May Bhaga be auspicious to us, and may our praise be auspicious; may Puraṃdhi be auspicious to us, and may riches be auspicious to us.
May the praise of the true and well-guided one be auspicious to us, and may Aryaman, born of many, be auspicious to us.
May Dhātṛ be auspicious to us, and may the Sustainer be auspicious to us; may the far-reaching [goddess] be auspicious to us with her self-sustaining powers.
May the two vast worlds, heaven and earth, be auspicious; may the mountain be auspicious to us; may the propitious invocations of the gods be auspicious to us.
May Agni, with his face of light, be auspicious to us; may Mitra and Varuṇa and the Aśvins be auspicious to us.
May the good deeds of the doers of good be auspicious to us; may the swift wind blow auspiciously upon us.
May Heaven and Earth be auspicious for us at our first invocation; may the intermediate space be auspicious for us to behold.
May the plants and the trees be auspicious for us; may the victorious Lord of the Atmosphere be auspicious for us.
May the god Indra with the Vasus be auspicious for us, and may Varuṇa, the one of fair praise, be auspicious with the Ādityas.
May the healing Rudra with his Rudras be auspicious to us; may Tvaṣṭṛ with the divine dames hear us here for our welfare.
(7) May Soma be auspicious to us, may the sacred prayer be auspicious to us; may the pressing-stones be auspicious to us, and may the sacrifices be auspicious.
(8) May the fixing of the sacrificial posts be auspicious to us; may the plants be auspicious to us, and may the altar be auspicious. (9)
May the far-seeing Sūrya rise for our welfare; may the four quarters of space be auspicious for us.
May the firm mountains be auspicious for us, and may the rivers and the waters be for our well-being.
(8) May Aditi be auspicious to us through her sacred laws, and may the Maruts, who sing beautiful hymns, be auspicious to us. (9)
May Viṣṇu be auspicious to us, and may Pūṣan be auspicious to us; may the means of protection be auspicious to us, and may Vāyu be auspicious.
May the divine Savitṛ, our protector, be auspicious to us; may the dawns, shining forth, be auspicious to us.
May Parjanya be auspicious to our offspring, and may the Lord of the Field be a source of well-being and auspiciousness to us.
May the lords of truth be auspicious to us; may our coursers be auspicious and our cattle be auspicious.
May the Ṛbhus, the skillful-handed doers of good deeds, be auspicious to us; may the Fathers be auspicious to us at our invocations.
May the All-Gods, the gods, be auspicious to us; may Sarasvatī together with our prayers be auspicious.

(19.11.2.c) May those who attack us be appeased; may those who bestow gifts be appeased; may the divine ones and the earthly ones be auspicious to us; may the waters be auspicious to us. 2 (19.11.3’) May the god Aja Ekapād be auspicious to us; may Ahi Budhnya be auspicious, and may the ocean be auspicious.
(19.11.3.c) May the son of the waters, the protector, be auspicious to us; may Pṛśni, whose guardians are the gods, be auspicious to us. 3

May the Ādityas, Rudras, and Vasus take pleasure in this newly fashioned prayer being performed. May those who dwell in heaven, those on earth, those born of the cow, and those worthy of sacrifice hear us.
Those who are the priests of the gods, worthy of sacrifice, the venerable ones of Manu, the immortal knowers of the Eternal Order (*ṛta*).
May they grant us wide-striding space today; do you all protect us always with your blessings.
(5) May that be so, O Mitra and Varuṇa; may that be so, O Agni. May this be for us a source of well-being and peace when recited.
May we attain a firm footing and a secure standing. Homage to the great heavenly abode! (6)
(19.12.1) Dawn rolls away the darkness of her sister by her noble birth, turning back her path.
Through this, may we win god-appointed strength; may we rejoice for a hundred winters, blessed with heroic sons.
(19.13.1) Indra’s two arms are sturdy and virile; these two wonderful bulls are victorious.
(19.13.1.c) I shall yoke those two first when the time for union has come, by which the light of the Asuras was won.
(19.13.2’) Swift, sharpening his horns like a terrible bull, the striker, the agitator of the peoples; the roaring, unblinking, sole hero Indra conquered a hundred armies at once.
(19.13.2.c) The roaring, unblinking, sole hero Indra conquered a hundred armies at once.
With him who is the thunderer, the unblinking, the victorious, the invincible, the unshakable, the bold—
with that Indra, O men, conquer and prevail in battle, with the bull who holds arrows in his hand.
He, the wielder of arrows, he who carries quivers, the controller, the one who joins together in combat— Indra, with his host.
(19.13.4.c) Conqueror of the gathered host, Soma-drinker, strong-armed, with a formidable bow, shooting with well-aimed arrows;
(19.13.5.a) known for his strength, steadfast, preeminent hero, victorious, powerful, enduring, fierce;
(19.13.5.c) a hero who overcomes, a warrior who triumphs, winning power—O Indra, mount your victorious, cattle-winning chariot!

Rejoice after this hero; O friends, rally together after the fierce Indra—him who conquers hosts, who wins cattle, whose arm wields the thunderbolt, who is victorious in the race, and who crushes with his might.
6 Piercing through the cow-pens with force, the fierce Indra, the giver, possessing a hundredfold wrath, [advances]. 7
(19.13.7.c) May Duścyavana, the subduer of hostile armies, the invincible, protect our troops in the battles!
(19.13.8’) O Bṛhaspati, fly around with your chariot, slayer of demons, driving away our enemies;
shattering the foes and crushing the adversaries, be the protector of our bodies!
May Indra be their leader; may Bṛhaspati, the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*), the sacrifice, and Soma go before them.
Let the Maruts march in the midst of the divine armies as they shatter [the enemy] and conquer.
[The host] of the bull Indra, of King Varuṇa, of the Ādityas, and of the Maruts is formidable.
The shout of the high-minded gods, who cause the world to tremble, has risen up as they triumph.
(10) May Indra be on our side when our banners meet; may those arrows which are ours be victorious.
May our heroes prevail; O gods, protect us in our invocations! (11)
I have come to this most excellent end; may Heaven and Earth be auspicious for me.
May the quarters be free from rivals for me; we truly do not hate you; let there be safety for us.
O Indra, from whatever we fear, from that make us fearless.
O Maghavan, grant us success; with your aids, strike down our enemies and our adversaries.
We invoke Indra, the one who grants prosperity; may we prosper in our bipeds and quadrupeds.
Let not hostile armies press upon us; O Indra, utterly destroy those who seek to harm us from every side.
Indra is our protector, the slayer of Vṛtra, the far-expanding, the most excellent. May he be our guardian from the furthest point, may he be from the middle; may he be behind us and before us.
O Knower, lead us to a wide world—toward the light of heaven, toward fearlessness, and toward well-being.
(19.15.4.c) O Indra, may we dwell under the protection of your two mighty, ancient, and vast arms.

(19.15.5.a) May the mid-region grant us fearlessness; may both these, heaven and earth, grant us fearlessness. (19.15.5.c) May there be fearlessness from behind, fearlessness from before, and fearlessness from above and below for us. (19.15.5.e) May there be fearlessness for us.
Fearlessness from friend and fearlessness from foe; fearlessness from kinsman and fearlessness for those before us;
fearlessness by night and fearlessness by day—may all the quarters become my friends.
May there be freedom from rivals in front, and may fearlessness be established behind us.
May Savitṛ protect me from the south; may the Lord of Might protect me from the north.
May the Ādityas guard me from heaven, and the fires guard me from the earth.
May Indra and Agni protect me from the front, and may the Aśvins grant me shelter on both sides.
(19.16.2.e) May Jātavedas, the inviolable one, protect me from the side; may the creators of beings be my armor on every side.
2 (19.17.1’) May Agni with the Vasus protect me from the east. In that stride, in that refuge, I enter that fortress.
(19.17.1.c) May he protect me; may he guard me. To him I entrust myself. Svāhā! 1

May Vāyu protect me from this direction by means of the intermediate space; in that step, in that refuge, I enter that fortress. May he protect me, may he guard me; unto him I entrust myself. Svāhā! May Soma protect me from the southern direction by means of the Rudras; in that step, in that refuge, I enter that fortress.
(19.17.3.c) May he protect me; may he guard me. To him I entrust myself. Svāhā!
(19.17.4’) May Varuṇa, together with the Ādityas, protect me from this direction. In that stride, in that refuge, I enter that fortress.
(19.17.4.c) May he protect me; may he guard me. To him I entrust myself. Svāhā!

(19.17.5) May Sūrya protect me from heaven and earth, from the western quarter. In him I step; in him I rest; to that fortress I go. May he protect me; may he guard me. To him I entrust myself. Svāhā! (19.17.6) May the waters rich in herbs protect me from this quarter. In them I step; in them I rest; to that fortress I go.
(19.17.6.c) May they protect me; may they guard me; to them I entrust myself—*svāhā*!

(19.17.7’) May Viśvakarman with the Seven Seers protect me from the northern quarter. In that stride, in that refuge, I enter that fortress. (19.17.7.c) May he protect me; may he guard me; to him I entrust myself—*svāhā*!
May Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, protect me from this direction. In that stride, in that refuge, I enter that fortress.
May he protect me; may he guard me. To him I entrust myself. Svāhā!
May Prajāpati, the possessor of procreative power, together with the firm foundation, protect me from the fixed direction. In that stride, in that refuge, I enter that fortress.
Raimi! May he protect me; may he guard me. To him I entrust myself. Svāhā!
(9) Bṛhaspati, together with all the gods, may he protect me from the upward direction. In that stride, in that refuge, I enter that fortress. (10)
May he protect me; may he guard me. To him I entrust myself. Svāhā!
May they encounter Agni, the possessor of wealth—those malicious ones who would attack me from the eastern direction.
(19.18.2’) May they encounter Vāyu accompanied by the intermediate space— those malicious ones who from this quarter seek to harm me. (19.18.3’) May they encounter Soma accompanied by Rudra.
(19.18.3.c) Those malevolent ones who would attack me from the southern direction— (19.18.4.a) let them encounter Varuṇa, accompanied by the Ādityas;
(19.18.4.c) those malevolent ones who would attack me from this direction.
(19.18.5) May the sun reach you, together with heaven and earth— those malevolent ones who, from the western quarter, seek to harm me.
(19.18.6) May the waters rich in herbs reach you.
(19.18.6.c) Those malevolent ones who would attack me from this direction—
(19.18.7.a) let them encounter Viśvakarman accompanied by the Seven Seers.
(19.18.7.c) Those malevolent ones who would attack me from the northern direction—
(19.18.8) May they strike Indra accompanied by the Maruts— those malevolent ones who would attack me from this direction.
(19.18.9) May they strike Prajāpati, the procreative one.
(19.18.9.c) Those malicious ones who would attack me from the fixed quarter—
(19.18.10.a) may they encounter Bṛhaspati accompanied by all the gods—
(19.18.10.c) those malicious ones who would attack me from the upward quarter.
Mitra rose up from the earth; I lead you toward that fortress.
Enter it, enter into it; may it grant you shelter and protection.
Vāyu rose up through the mid-air; I lead you toward that fortress.
Enter it; enter into it deeply. May it grant you both protection and armor.
Sūrya has ascended from the sky; I lead you toward that fortress.
Enter it; enter into it deeply. May it grant you both protection and armor.
The Moon rose up with the constellations; that fortress I lead you toward.
Enter it, enter into it; may it grant you both shelter and protection.
Soma rose up with the plants; that fortress I lead you toward.
Enter it; enter into it! May it grant you both shelter and protection.
(5) The sacrifice ascended with the sacrificial fees; I lead you toward that fortress.
Enter it; enter into it! May it grant you both shelter and protection. (6)
The ocean has emerged with the rivers; I lead you toward that city. Enter it, enter it deeply; may it grant you protection and armor.
(7) The sacred word (*brahman*) has emerged with those practicing the student life (*brahmacārin*); I lead you toward that city. (8)
(19.19.8.c) Enter it, enter into it; may it grant you both shelter and protection.
(19.19.9.a) Indra ascended with heroic power; I lead you toward that fortress.
(19.19.9.c) Enter it, enter into it; may it grant you both shelter and protection.
The gods ascended by means of the nectar; I lead you toward that fortress.
Enter it, enter it fully; may it grant you protection and armor.
Prajāpati ascended with his creatures; I lead you toward that fortress.
(19.19.11.c) Enter it, enter into it; may it grant you both shelter and protection.
‖11‖ (19.20.1’) Indra, Agni, Dhātṛ, Savitṛ, and Bṛhaspati have cast away the human weapon of death;
(19.20.1.c) may King Soma, Varuṇa, the Aśvins, Yama, and Pūṣan protect us from death. ‖1‖
Whatever [armors] Prajāpati, the Lord of the world, and Mātariśvan fashioned for the sake of creatures—
those which clothe the intermediate directions and the cardinal quarters— may those many armors be mine. Those armors which the gods, the lords of heaven, wearing bodies, bound upon their limbs.
(19.20.3.c) That armor which Indra fashioned—may it protect us from every side.
(19.20.4’) May Heaven and Earth be my armor; may the Day be my armor, and the Sun my armor.
(19.20.4.c) May all the gods grant me armor; let no adversary come upon me.
The Gāyatrī, Uṣṇih, Anuṣṭubh, Bṛhatī, Paṅkti, Triṣṭubh, and Jagatī [are the meters] for the Jagatī.

To the green ones, svāhā!
(19.22.6) Svāhā to the petty ones! (19.22.7) Svāhā to those who move in succession!
(19.22.8) Svāhā to the first conchs!

To the northern ones, svāhā!

(19.22.19) Svāhā to the two separate thousands!

(19.22.21’) The powers were gathered with Brahmā as the eldest; Brahmā extended the supreme heaven at the beginning.

With that by which the gods encompassed the god Savitṛ,
with that, O Brahmaṇaspati, do you encompass this man for the sake of the kingdom.
Encompass this Indra for long life and for great sovereignty.
So that you may lead him to old age, let him remain awake for a long time within his dominion. Place this Indra around for long life and for great hearing,
so that you may lead him to old age, and he may remain awake for a long time within his hearing.
Clothe him, clothe him with splendor; make him one who dies of old age, grant him long life.
Bṛhaspati has bestowed this garment upon King Soma that he may put it on.
Go well to old age, put on the garment, and become a protector against the curses of the young cows.
May you live for a hundred abundant autumns, and clothe yourself in the increase of wealth.
(5) You have put on this garment for well-being; you have become a protector against curses and a guardian of waters.
May you live for a hundred abundant autumns, and as a lovely one, may you distribute riches while living. (6)
In every endeavor, in every contest, we, as friends, invoke the most powerful Indra for our protection.
O golden-hued, undecaying one, endowed with heroic sons, enter into union with offspring, having overcome old age and death.
(19.24.8.c) This Agni has said, and Soma has said it; Bṛhaspati, Savitṛ, and Indra have said it.
(19.25.1’) I yoke you with the mind of one who is unwearied, and with that of the first. (19.25.1.c) Be a carrier up the slope; having carried up, run back again.
The immortal gold that was produced from Agni, which was placed among mortals—only he who knows it truly deserves it; he who wears it becomes one whose death is old age.
That gold which is bright like the sun, which the progeny-bearing men of old desired—
(19.26.2.c) He unites you, who are bright, with splendor; he who wears [this] becomes long-lived.
(19.26.3’) For life, for splendor, for vigor, and for strength— (19.26.3.c) so that by the brilliance of gold you may shine forth among the people.
That which King Varuṇa knows, that which the god Bṛhaspati knows, and that which Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra, knows—may that be for you a source of long life; may that be for you a source of splendor.
May the bull protect you with cows; may the stallion protect you with swift horses.
May Vāyu protect you with the sacred word (*brahman*); may Indra protect you with his powers (*indriya*).
(1) May Soma protect you with the plants; may Sūrya protect you with the constellations. May Candra, the slayer of Vṛtra, protect you from the months; may Vāta guard you with his breath. (2)
Three heavens, three earths, three intermediate spaces, and four oceans;
they call the threefold hymn the threefold waters—may these protect you with the threefold and by means of the threefold.
Three firmaments, three oceans, three radiances, and three celestial summits.
I fashion three Mātariśvans and three Sūryas as guardians.
(4) I sprinkle you with ghee, O Agni, increasing you with clarified butter.
May the deceivers not harm the breath of Agni, of the Moon, and of the Sun. (5)
(19.27.6) Let not the deceivers harm your out-breath, nor your in-breath, nor your vigor. O radiant gods, possessors of all wealth, run with your divine power!
(19.27.7) Vāta unites Agni with the out-breath; he is joined with the out-breath.
(19.27.7.c) By means of breath, the gods generated the sun, which faces every direction. (19.27.8.a) Through life, live the life of those who grant life; being long-lived, live, do not die!
(19.27.8.c) By means of breath, live the life of those possessed of self; do not fall under the power of death.

The treasure deposited by the gods, which Indra discovered by means of the paths traveled by the gods—the waters guarded that gold with their triple-layered forms; may they protect you with their triple-layered forms, with their triple-layered protections. 9 The thirty-three deities and the three powers, acting with affection, have guarded [the treasure] within the waters. 10
Whatever gold is upon this moon, with that may he perform heroic deeds.
(10) O gods who are eleven in heaven, you gods, enjoy this oblation!
(11) O gods who are eleven in the intermediate space, you gods, enjoy this oblation! (12)
O gods who are eleven upon the earth, you gods, enjoy this oblation!
13 Make us free from rivals in the east and grant us security in the west;
may Savitṛ protect me from the south, and the Lord of Might from the north. 14
May the Ādityas protect me from heaven; may the fires protect me from the earth.

May Indra and Agni protect me from the front; may the Aśvins grant me shelter on both sides. May the inviolable Jātavedas protect me from the transverse direction; may the creators of beings be my armor on every side.
I bind this amulet for you for long life and for splendor—
this *darbha* grass, which crushes rivals and burns the heart of the enemy.
Burning the hearts of those who hate you, it scorches the minds of your foes.
O Darbha, like the *gharma* vessel, do thou burn all those of evil heart, scorching them thoroughly.
O Darbha, O jewel, heating like the *gharma*, do thou consume the enemies;
rend the hearts of our rivals as Indra shattered the strength of Virocana.
O Darbha, pierce the hearts of my rivals, O amulet of those who hate me!
As the rising sun [strips] the skin from the earth, so cause their heads to fall apart!
O Darbha, pierce my rivals; pierce those who array themselves against me in battle!
(19.28.5.c) Shatter all my ill-wishers, shatter my enemies, O amulet!
(19.28.6’) Cut down my rivals, O *darbha* grass; cut down those who array themselves against me in battle! Cut down all my ill-wishers, cut down my enemies, O amulet!
(19.28.7) O Darbha, cut down my rivals; cut down those who attack me in battle. Cut down all those of evil heart; cut down those who hate me, O amulet!
(19.28.8) Tear asunder my rivals, O Darbha; tear asunder those who attack me in battle.

(19.28.8.c) Cut away all those of evil heart for me; cut away my enemies, O amulet! (19.28.9.a) Carve up my rivals, O *darbha* grass; carve up those who advance against me in battle; (19.28.9.c) carve up all those of evil heart for me; carve up my enemies, O amulet! (19.28.9)
Pierce my rivals with the *darbha* grass; pierce those who array themselves against me.
Pierce all those of evil heart; pierce my enemies, O amulet!
Drive away my rivals with the *darbha* grass; drive away those who array themselves against me.
Cast down all those of evil heart for me; cast down my enemies, O amulet!
(1) Pierce my rivals, O *darbha* grass; pierce those who array themselves against me in battle! Pierce all those of evil heart for me; pierce my enemies, O amulet! (2)
(19.29.3) O Darbha, hold back my rivals; hold back those who attack me in battle. Hold back all those of evil heart; hold back my enemies, O amulet!
(19.29.4) Crush my rivals, O Darbha; crush those who attack me in battle.
(19.29.4.c) Grind all those of evil heart for me; grind my enemies, O amulet!
(19.29.5.a) Churn up my rivals, O *darbha* grass; churn up those who attack me in battle! (19.29.5.c) Churn up all those of evil heart for me; churn up my enemies, O amulet!
(19.29.6) Crush my rivals, O Darbha; crush those who advance against me in battle. Crush all who are ill-disposed toward me; crush my enemies, O Amulet!
(19.29.7) Burn my rivals, O Darbha; burn those who advance against me in battle.
Burn all those of evil heart toward me; burn my enemies, O amulet!
(7) Burn my rivals, O *darbha* grass; burn those who attack me in battle! Burn all those of evil heart toward me; burn my enemies, O amulet! (8)
Slay my rivals, O Darbha; slay those who attack me in battle.
Slay all those of evil heart toward me; slay my enemies, O amulet!
That which is your old age and death, O Darbha—let that be a hundredfold armor among your defenses.
(19.30.1.c) Having made this man armored with it, slay his rivals with your heroic powers.
(19.30.2’) A hundred are your *darbha*-armors; a thousand are your heroic powers.
(19.30.2.c) All the gods have given you over to him to wear for his preservation.
They call you the divine armor; O Darbha, they call you the Lord of Prayer (Brahmaṇaspati).
They say you are the armor of Indra; you protect the kingdoms.
O Darbha, you are the destroyer of rivals and the burner of the hearts of enemies.
I fashion for you this amulet, the increaser of dominion, the protector of the body.
When the ocean roared aloud together with Parjanya and the lightning, from that a golden drop arose; from that, the *darbha* grass was born.
May Savitṛ, the Ordainer, by means of an *audumbara* gem, bring about the increase of all cattle within my pen for one desiring prosperity.
May that Agni who is our *gārhapatya* fire become the lord of our cattle.

(19.31.2.c) May the *vṛsa* amulet made of udumbara wood unite me with nourishment. (19.31.3.a) May there be abundance of manure, fruitfulness, the ancestral offering (*svadhā*), and refreshing food (*irā*) in our house;
(19.31.3.c) by the splendor of the udumbara tree, may Dhātṛ bestow prosperity upon me.
Whatever food there is of the two-footed and the four-footed, whatever juices there are— I grasp the abundance of these, wearing the *audumbara* amulet.
I have grasped the nourishment of cattle, both four-footed and two-footed, and whatever grain there is.
May Bṛhaspati and Savitṛ bestow upon me the milk of cattle and the sap of plants.
(5) May I be the lord of cattle; may the Lord of Prosperity bestow nourishment upon me.
May the Udumbara amulet grant riches unto me. (6)
May the *mauḍumbára* amulet come to me with progeny and with wealth;
may the amulet, impelled by Indra, come to me together with splendor.
May the divine amulet, the slayer of rivals, a winner of wealth, [come] for the winning of wealth.
May he bestow abundance of livestock and prosperity of cattle.
Just as you, O Lord of the Forest, were born in the beginning together with nourishment,
so may Sarasvatī grant me an increase of wealth.
May Sarasvatī bring me wealth, abundance of milk, and grain;
may Sinīvālī bring them hither, as does this amulet made of udumbara wood.
You are the lord of amulets, you are the bull; the Lord of Prosperity has produced nourishment within you.
(19.31.11.c) In you are these strengths and all riches; you are made of udumbara wood. As such, from afar, drive away from us the enemy, the lack of wisdom, and hunger.
11 (19.31.12’) You are a leader; having risen as a leader, you have been consecrated—sprinkle me with splendor! You are brilliance; bestow brilliance upon me. You are wealth; grant me wealth. 12

(19.31.13’) You are nourishment; anoint me with nourishment. As one who performs the domestic sacrifice, make me the master of the house. (19.31.13.c) O you who are made of Udumbara wood, bestow wealth upon us; grant us prosperity consisting of all heroic sons. For the increase of riches, I fasten you on myself. ||1 3||
This heroic amulet of udumbara wood is bound upon the hero.
May it provide us with a honey-sweet gain and bestow upon us wealth consisting of all-heroic sons.
With a hundred stalks, difficult to shake, a thousand leaves, and most excellent, may it protect us.
The Darbha grass that is a formidable herb— this I bind upon you for the sake of long life.
They do not shave his hair, nor do they strike him on the chest,
for whom he provides protection with a Darbha blade whose leaf remains unbroken.
O herb, your tuft is in heaven; you are established upon the earth.
Through you, with your thousand stalks, we increase our lifespan.
He has pierced through the three heavens and these three earths as well.
(19.32.4.c) With you as my ally, O Durhārda, I shall cut off the tongues with my words.
(19.32.5.a) You are the conqueror; I am the victorious one. (19.32.5.c) Having both become powerful, may we overcome our rivals.
Overpower our adversary; overpower those who attack us in battle. Overpower all the evil-hearted ones, and make many for me who are well-disposed.
With the darbha grass, born of the gods, which is ever a pillar reaching to heaven—
(19.32.7.c) By that means, may I always consume people and continue to consume them.
(19.32.8’) O Darbha, make me dear to the Brahmin and the Kṣatriya, to the Śūdra and the Ārya;
(19.32.8.c) and to whomever we desire, and to every one who perceives clearly.
He who, being born, made the earth firm, who propped up the mid-air and the heaven—
he whom no evil found while he was bearing [the world], may this Darbha grass be for us today as Varuṇa is in heaven.
The slayer of rivals, hundred-stalked and victorious, it became the first among plants.
May this *darbha* protect us on every side; with it may I overcome the armies of those who attack us.

Worth a thousand, possessing a hundred stalks, full of sap, the fire of the waters, the royal consecration (*rājasūya*) of plants—may this *darbha* protect us on every side; may the divine amulet unite us with long life.

Drawn from clarified butter, rich in honey, full of milk, a firm support of the earth, unshakable yet causing [the enemy] to fall—driving away rivals and casting them down, O Darbha grass, grow with the power of the great!
You shall surpass the earth with your might; you sit as a beautiful one upon the sacrificial altar during the rite.

With darbha grass you shall perform heroic deeds; bearing darbha within yourself, do not falter.
Standing firm with splendor, surpass all others and shine like the sun in the four quarters.
You are Jaṅgiḍa, you are the protector Jaṅgiḍa, you are the deliverer Jaṅgiḍa.

May Jaṅgiḍa protect all of us—both bipeds and quadrupeds. (1) May Jaṅgiḍa, with his splendor, separate and render powerless all those who are the ninety-three Gṛtsyas and the hundred makers of sorcery. (2)
(19.34.3) Tasteless and artificial is the roar; tasteless are the seven decays. O Jaṅgiḍa, drive away excessive longing; strike it down like an archer his arrow.
(19.34.4) This indeed is the destroyer of witchcraft, and likewise the destroyer of the enemy.
(19.34.4.c) And may the powerful Jaṅgiḍa extend our lifespans.
(19.34.5.a) May that greatness of Jaṅgiḍa protect us on every side,
(19.34.5.c) by which he overcomes Viṣkandha and Saṃskandha with his own might.
The gods have established you thrice upon the earth;
the ancient Brahmins know you as Aṅgiras. Neither the plants of old nor those that are new surpass you.
The formidable *jaṅgiḍa* is a dispeller of obstacles, a protection on all sides, and most auspicious.
(7) Then, O Blessed One, regarding the *jaṅgiḍa* of immeasurable power:
formerly, when the fierce ones were about to devour you, Upendra bestowed his own heroism upon it. (8)
O Lord of the Forest, Indra, the fierce one, has bestowed his vigor upon you.
Drive away all diseases; O Herb, slay the demons!
[9] The wasting disease, the dispersing disease, the balāsa, and the pain of the back—[10]
May Jaṅgiḍa render the autumnal fever powerless.
(19.34.10c) The seers, uttering the name of Indra, gave the Jaṅgiḍa plant;
it is that which the gods made into a medicine in the beginning, the destroyer of *viṣkandha*. (19.35.1)
May that Jaṅgiḍa protect us, like a guardian of wealth over riches—
he whom the gods and the brahmins made into a complete protection against the malevolent.
May he [ward off] the evil-hearted one, the terrible eye, and the arrival of the doer of evil.
O thousand-eyed one, destroy them with your awakening; you, Jaṅgiḍa, are our complete protection.
From heaven protect me, from earth protect me, from the intermediate space protect me, and from the plants protect me.
From what has been and from what is to be, from every direction let Jaṅgiḍa protect us.
Whatever wasting diseases are created by the gods, and whatever others have arisen—
may Jaṅgiḍa, the possessor of all remedies, render them all sapless.
Śatavāra has destroyed the consumptions and the demons with his splendor.
Ascending with splendor, this jewel drives away evil names. (1) With its two horns it pushes back the *rakṣas*, and with its base it repels the sorceresses;
with its middle it strikes down consumption (*yakṣman*); no evil overcomes it. (2)
The consumption-diseases, whether small or great, and those that are noisy—
all those with evil names, the hundred-protecting amulet has destroyed them. It has brought forth a hundred heroes and has scattered away a hundred consumption-diseases.
Having struck down all those of evil name, he shakes off the *rakṣases*.
This golden-horned bull, the *śātavāra* amulet,
having trampled all those of evil name, has stepped over the *rakṣases*.
A hundred of the ill-named ones, a hundred Gandharvas and Apsarases, a hundred of those who follow the hare—these I ward off with the hundredfold filter.
This splendor given by Agni has come to me: glory, renown, power, vigor, vitality, and strength.
May Agni bestow upon me those thirty-three heroic powers. Bestow splendor upon my body, along with vigor, vitality, and strength.
For the sake of sensory power, for ritual action, and for heroism, I accept you for a hundred autumns.
For nourishment, for strength, for vigor, for power, for supremacy,
and for the sustenance of the kingdom, I carry you around for a hundred autumns.
For the seasons, for the seasonal periods, for the months, and for the years, I carry you around.
I sacrifice to Dhātṛ, Vidhātṛ, Samṛdh, and the Lord of Beings.
Diseases do not obstruct him, nor does a curse reach him,
whom the fragrant scent of the healing guggulu resin reaches.
Therefore, the consumptive diseases flee in all directions like deer or horses;
whether it be *gulgulu* from the Indus or that which comes from the sea,
I have grasped the names of both for his safety.
May the divine *kuṣṭha*, the protector, come from the Himalayas;
destroy every *takman* and all sorceresses.
O *kuṣṭha*, you have three names: *nadyamāra*, *nadyāriṣa*, and [the third].
(19.39.2.c) May this man not come to harm by the river, (19.39.2.e) for whom I address you, evening and morning, and also by day.
(19.39.3’) Jīvalā is the name of your mother; Jīvanta is the name of your father.
(19.39.3.c) May this man not suffer harm from the river,

for whom I pronounce you [a protection] in the evening, in the morning, and likewise by day. (19.39.4’) You are the highest of plants, like a bull among moving creatures, like a tiger among beasts of prey.
(19.39.4.c) May this man not come to harm from the river,
(19.39.4.e) for whom I proclaim you, evening and morning, and also by day.
(19.39.5’) Three times from the Śambus and the Aṅgirases, three times from the Ādityas— around [him].
Born thrice from the Viśvedevas,
that Kuṣṭha, the universal healer, stands together with Soma.
The Aśvattha tree, the abode of the gods, is in the third heaven from here.
Therein was the manifestation of the immortal; from that, Kuṣṭha was born.
That Kuṣṭha, the universal remedy, stands together with Soma.
A golden ship with golden moorings moved in the sky.
There, at the sight of the nectar, Kuṣṭha was born from that;
that Kuṣṭha, the universal remedy, stands together with Soma.
Where there is the place of our descent, where the summit of the Himavat is located.
Therein was the manifestation of immortality; from that, Kuṣṭha was born.
That Kuṣṭha, the universal remedy, stands together with Soma.
O Kuṣṭha, you whom the ancient Ikṣvāku knew, or you whom the beloved [prince] knew—
O Vasu, whatever you shall consume, by that you are the all-healing one.
The headache, the tertian fever, the constant, and the annual;
drive away the *takman* with your universal power, sending it far down below.

Whatever flaw there is in my mind and whatever in my speech—Sarasvatī has gone to the wrathful one; may Bṛhaspati, in agreement with all the gods, restore that for me. O Waters, do not disturb our wisdom nor our sacred formulation.
(19.40.2.c) Flow forth, you who are ready to swell; I have been invoked, wise and full of splendor.
(19.40.3’) Do not harm our wisdom, nor our consecration, nor our ascetic fervor.
May they be auspicious and bring us peace for our life; may the Mothers be gracious to us.
May that luminous power which has carried us across the darkness, O Aśvins—
may it grant us such nourishment.
Seeking what is auspicious and finding the light of heaven, the seers in the beginning sat down to austerity and consecration.
(19.41.1.c) Therefore, may the gods grant him the kingdom, strength, and vital power that have been produced.
‖1‖ (19.42.1’) The *brahman* is the *hotṛ*, the *brahman* is the sacrifice; by the *brahman* are the sacrificial posts measured.
(19.42.1.c) The *adhvaryu* is born from the *brahman*; from the *brahman* comes the hidden oblation. ‖1‖
The *sruk* ladles are filled with clarified butter through the *brahman*; by the *brahman* the altar is raised.
The *brahman* is the essence of the sacrifice, as are the officiating priests who prepare the oblations.
To the immolator, *svāhā*!
To him who releases from distress, I offer my inspired thought; seeking his favor, I choose the benevolence of the one who protects well.
O Indra, accept this oblation; may the desires of the sacrificer come true.
[3] To the one who releases from distress, the bull of those worthy of sacrifice, the first among the rites, shining forth—
(19.42.4.c) I invoke the Son of the Waters, O Aśvins; through your power, grant me wisdom, power, and vigor.
(19.43.1’) Where those who know the sacred formulation go, together with consecration and austerity—may Agni lead me there; may Agni bestow intelligence upon me.
(19.43.1.e) To Agni, svāhā!
‖1‖ (19.43.2’) Where those who know Brahman go by means of initiation and austerity, (19.43.2.c) may Vāyu lead me there; may Vāyu sustain my vital breaths. To Vāyu, svāhā! ‖2‖
Where those who know Brahman go by means of initiation and austerity—may Sūrya lead me there; may Sūrya bestow sight upon me. Svāhā to Sūrya! 3.3.3.19.43.3e.
Where those who know Brahman go by means of initiation and austerity—may Candra lead me there; may Candra bestow his mind upon me. Svāhā to Candra! 4.43.4e ||4||
Where those who know Brahman go by means of initiation and austerity—may Soma lead me there; may Soma bestow milk upon me. Svāhā to Soma! 5.5.19.43.5–e.
Where those who know Brahman go by means of initiation and austerity—may Indra lead me there; may Indra bestow strength upon me. Svāhā to Indra! 6.
Where those who know Brahman go by means of initiation and austerity—may the waters lead me there; may immortality attend me. Svāhā to the waters! 7.7.19.43.7e.

Therefore, O ointment, grant us well-being; may the waters bring peace and security.
(19.44.2) Whatever jaundice, wasting disease, joint-pain, or neuralgia there may be—

(19.44.2.c) May this ointment drive all consumption out from your limbs.
