Upward those rays of light bear him, the god Jātavedas,
the Sun, so that everyone may behold him.
Away go those stars with the nights, like thieves in the darkness.
To the hero, the all-seeing one.
(14) His heralds have become visible, his rays extending over the people, shining like fires. (15)
O Sūrya, you are the deliverer, visible to all, the maker of light;
you illuminate the entire radiant realm.
Facing the clans of the gods, facing the human tribes, you rise up.

(20.47.17.c) Turning back, he gazes upon the whole world of light. (20.47.18’) O Purifier, with that eye wherewith thou beholdest the active people, O Varuṇa, thou seest them. (20.47.18.c) O Varuṇa, thou seest them.
You rise across the sky, through the broad expanse, measuring out the day with your rays; O Sūrya, you behold all living beings. Seven bay horses carry you in your chariot, O divine Sūrya.
(20.47.20.c) The far-seeing one with flaming hair.
20. (20.47.21’) The Sun has yoked the seven bright mares, the daughters of his chariot;
with them, self-yoked, he goes forth. 21.
The eager songs sprinkle you with splendor,
as milch-cows low toward their calf. These radiant ones flow forth, blending milk with splendor.
Born as birth is conceived by the heart.
O you who flow with the thunderbolt, bringing fame to the dying man,
bring to me long life, ghee, and milk.
This spotted bull has stepped forth; he has settled before his mother, and as he moves toward the light, he approaches his father.
He moves within the luminous realms, breathing out from his breath.
The buffalo has revealed the sun.
5 He rules over thirty domains; the bird has taken his stand with speech, day after day at the break of dawn. 6
When the Śakras have mounted their voice, you two seek to win the mid-air;
the bull has gladdened the gods together.
Śakra has spoken the invincible word; speak forth, O invincible one!
Most bountiful, he has rejoiced in heaven.
Śakra, invincible, rules over speech according to the ordinances of the sacred law;
exhilarated, he has spread upon the sacrificial grass.
We praise with songs that Indra for you— the wondrous subduer of the assailants, who rejoices in the exhilarating juice of wealth— just as cows low toward their calf in the stalls.
He dwells in heaven, the bounteous giver, encompassed by powers, possessing manifold nourishment like a mountain.
We quickly implore for food accompanied by cattle, consisting of hundreds and thousands.
I beg of you that heroic power, that sacred prayer (*brahman*) for the sake of primordial awareness,
by which you protected the *yatis* and Bhr̥gu when the prize was staked, and by which you aided Praskaṇva.
That by which you released the great waters toward the ocean—that, O Indra, is your virile power.
That greatness of his is not to be attained all at once, he whom the two worlds have shouted after in praise.
1. What newest hymn of the *atasī* plants shall the mortal sing to the swift one?
(20.50.1.c) Surely those who praise his majesty and his sovereign power have not attained the heavenly light.
(20.50.2’) When shall they, praising him, act according to the sacred law among the gods? Who is the seer, who is the inspired poet that he is honored?
When, O Indra Maghavan, will you come to the call of the one who presses the Soma, and when to the one who praises you?
Sing forth to Indra, the giver of goodly wealth, as he is known to be—he, the Maghavan, possessor of many riches, who bestows gifts upon his singers as if by the thousands.
Like one with a hundred armies, he advances boldly; he slays the Vṛtras for the sake of the donor.
Like streams from a mountain, the gifts of him who nourishes many flow forth abundantly.
Sing forth for our protection to Śakra, the far-renowned and bounteous giver,
who bestows desirable wealth upon the one who presses the soma and praises him, as if by the thousands.
His missiles are hundredfold and invincible; the great impetuous powers of Indra swell like a mountain rich in nourishment when the pressed juices have exhilarated him.
We, having prepared the sacrificial grass, possessing the pressed soma, call upon you just as waters flow.
At the springs of the Pavitra, O slayer of Vṛtra, the singers sit around thee.
When the Soma is pressed, O Vasu, the men who recite hymns sing aloud to thee alone.
When, O Indra, will you come to the pressed juice, thirsting for it as to your home, like a bellowing bull?
O bold one, with the Kaṇvas you have boldly struck down thousandfold booty; O Maghavan, most active among men, we quickly implore you for that golden-hued wealth consisting of cattle.
Who knows him when he drinks at the pressed juice? What vital strength does he bestow?
This one, exhilarated by the soma-juice, shatters the fortresses with his might, O fair-cheeked one. Like a wild elephant in its rutting season, he has assumed his course in many places.
No one can hold you back; come to the pressed juice! You move as a great being through your power.
He who, being fierce, unsubdued, and steadfast, is prepared for battle—
if Maghavan Indra hears the call of the singer, he will not stay away but shall come. In unison,
they have fashioned and brought forth Indra, the hero who overcomes all hostile armies, so that he may rule as king.

By his wisdom, he is the most excellent, the best at bringing down [the foe], the fierce, the strongest, the powerful, and the swift. (1) The singers have sung together to Indra for the drinking of Soma—that Lord of Heaven—for his increase, for he, whose vows are firm, is indeed endowed with might and with aids. (2)
(20.54.3’) With their vision, the inspired singers bow to the rim [of the wheel] and sing aloud to the Ram;
(20.54.3.c) you, O guileless and impetuous ones, are well-kindled even at our ear by those who chant the hymns.
(20.55.1’) That Indra, the bounteous and fierce one, who ever possesses irresistible powers—I call upon him repeatedly.
May the most generous one, worthy of sacrifice, turn toward us through our songs; may the wielder of the thunderbolt make all paths easy for us to attain wealth.
O Indra, those enjoyments which you brought from the Asuras for the sake of the light—O Maghavan, increase the singer of this hymn and those who have strewn the sacrificial grass before you.
O Indra, that horse and cow, the imperishable portion which you have held fast, bestow it upon the sacrificer who presses the soma and gives the sacrificial fee; do not place it with the miser.
Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra, has been strengthened by men for exhilaration and for power.
In great battles and even in small ones, we invoke him; may he further us in the contests for booty.
For you, O Hero, are worthy of armies; you are the one who bestows much. You are the strengthener even of the weak; you grant wealth to the sacrificer who presses the soma—abundant is your treasure.
When battles arise and wealth is staked for the bold, yoke your two bay steeds that drip with exhilaration. Whom will you slay? To whom will you grant riches? O Indra, grant us riches!
For at every draught of the soma, he of upright intent has given us herds of cattle.
Gather together with both hands the many hundreds of treasures; sharpen us for wealth and bring it to us!
Rejoice in the pressed juice, O hero, for the sake of strength and bounty;
for we know you as the possessor of abundant riches—we have sent forth our desires toward you—so be our protector!
O Indra, these people of yours nourish every desirable thing; for you, as the observer of men, know the wealth of those who do not give to the noble one. Bring that wealth to us!
(6) For our protection, [we call] the maker of beautiful forms, like a well-milking cow for the milker. (1)
Day after day we offer oblations.
(1) Come to our libations; O drinker of Soma, drink of the Soma!
The exhilaration of the wealthy one is indeed a giver of cattle. (2)
Then may we find your most intimate favors;
do not overlook us, but come to us! For our protection, drink the most powerful, glorious, and watchful [Soma].
O Indra, O Śatakratu, [drink] the Soma!
(4) O Śatakratu, those powers of yours which exist among the five peoples—O Indra, I choose them for you. (5)
O Indra, come; bestow upon us great renown and invincible splendor. We cause your strength to swell upward.
Come to us from nearby, O Śakra, or even from afar.
O wielder of the stone, come here from that world which is yours, O Indra!
(7) Indra indeed shall drive away even great fear; for he is steadfast and all-seeing. (8)
May Indra be gracious to us; may no evil reach us from behind;
may there be prosperity for us from the front.
May Indra grant us freedom from fear from all directions.
The conqueror of enemies, the one who observes all people.
10 Who knows him when he drinks at the pressed juice? What vital power does he bestow?
He is this very one who, exhilarated by the soma-plant, shatters the fortresses with his might, O fair-cheeked one. 11
Like a wild elephant in rut, he has established his course in many places.
No one can hold you back; come to the pressed juice! You move as a great one by your own might. He who is fierce, unsubdued, and steadfast, has been prepared for the battle.
(20.57.13.c) If Maghavan should hear the call of the praiser, may Indra not stay away but come hither.
13 (20.57.14’) We, having pressed the juice and trimmed the sacred grass like waters, O slayer of Vṛtra—(20.57.14.c)—the praisers sit around you at the outpourings of the filter. 14
O Vasu, when the pressed juice is offered, the men who recite hymns sing to you alone.
O Indra, when will you come to the pressed juice, thirsting for it as to your home, like a bellowing bull?
O Bold One, with the Kaṇvas, boldly strike out thousandfold booty.
O Maghavan, O far-seeing one, we quickly seek from you that golden-hued wealth consisting of cattle.
Like people looking up toward the sun, let all partake of Indra’s riches; for he bestows them upon every being born with his might. We look toward our allotted share as our due.
Praise him whose gifts are unimpaired, the giver of wealth; auspicious are the gifts of Indra.
He does not frustrate the desire of the one who serves him, but stirs his mind toward giving.
Truly, O Sūrya, you are great; truly, O Āditya, you are great.
The greatness of you who are great is praised; truly, O God, you are great.
(4) Indeed, O Sūrya, you are great in glory; you are entirely great, O God. By your greatness, you are the divine priest of the gods, the pervasive, invincible light. (5)
Upward rise these most honey-sweet songs, these hymns of praise, like chariots seeking booty, ever victorious, winning wealth, and providing inexhaustible aid.
Like the Kaṇvas and the Bhr̥gus, they have attained all their desire, even as the sun.
(20.59.2.c) The Āyus, magnifying Indra with their hymns of praise, the Priyamedhas have raised their voices.
(20.59.3.a) Truly, his portion overflows like the wealth of a victor;
(20.59.3.c) he who is Indra, the Lord of Bay Steeds—enemies cannot deceive him; he bestows skill upon the Soma-presser.
Place within those worthy of sacrifice a mantra that is unimpaired, well-established, and beautiful;
even many snares cannot overcome him who serves Indra with ritual action.
For such indeed you are—possessing heroic power, truly a hero, and steadfast.
(20.60.1.c) Thus may your mind be won over.
(20.60.2’) Thus has this gift been established by all the ordainers, O possessor of abundant wealth; even evil, O Indra, is with me.
(20.60.2.c) Even evil, O Indra, is with me.
O Lord of spoils, do not be sluggish like a weary priest;
exhilarate yourself with the pressed juice mixed with milk.
For thus indeed is his refreshing bounty—abundant, great, and rich in cattle.
(20.60.4.c) Like a branch ripened for the donor.
(20.60.5.a) For thus indeed are thy manifestations and aids, O Indra, for one such as I;
(20.60.5.c) they are instantly present for the donor.
For thus indeed are his desirable hymns and recitations to be chanted for Indra, for the drinking of the Soma.
We celebrate that exhilarating draught of thine, the bull-like one, victorious in battles.
O wielder of the stone, [we praise] you who create the world, who possess the splendor of the golden steeds— you by whom you discovered the lights for Āyu and for Manu;
rejoicing in this sacred grass (*barhis*), you shine forth.
Even now, those who offer hymns praise you as they did of old;
day by day, win the waters that have the bull as their lord.
Sing forth to him, the one invoked by many, the one praised by many.

O much-praised King, you alone strike down the Vṛtras, O Indra, so that we may attain victory and glory.
(20.61.6) Seeking your aid, we bring you, O matchless one, as if carrying a heavy burden, desiring your protection. (20.62.1)
In the battle for booty, we invoke the wondrous one.
Come near to us for aid in this rite, O fierce one, you who have come to us as our protector, being bold.
For we, your friends, have chosen you alone, O Indra, as our victorious helper.
I praise for you that Indra, the friend, for the sake of aid—him who brought this and that better thing here in the past.
(3) The Lord of the brave, master of bay horses, subduer of peoples; for he is indeed the one who has rejoiced [in the sacrifice]. (4)
(20.62.4.c) May that Maghavan bestow upon us, his worshippers, hundreds of cattle and horses.
(20.62.5’) Sing forth a lofty Sāman to Indra, the inspired, the great, the upholder of the Law, the wise, and the one worthy of praise.
(20.62.6) O Indra, you are the conqueror; you caused the sun to shine.
You are the maker of all, the god of all; you are great.
(20.62.7) Radiant with light, you went to the sky, to the luminous realm of heaven.
(20.62.7.c) Those gods, O Indra, have striven for your friendship. ||7|| (20.62.8.a) Sing forth unto him, who is invoked by many and praised by many;
(20.62.8.c) Invite the powerful Indra hither with your songs. ||8||
He whose great might is twofold upholds both heaven and earth, the mountains, the plains, the waters, and the sun by his virile power.
O much-praised one, you alone rule as king; you strike down the Vṛtras.
O Indra, come for victory and for the attainment of glory!
May we now bring these worlds to fulfillment, O Indra and all the gods.
May Indra, together with the Ādityas, fashion for us the sacrifice, our bodies, and our progeny.
May Indra, together with the Ādityas and the host of Maruts, be the protector of our bodies.
Having slain the Asuras, when the gods went forth, guarding their godhead. With their powers they brought the sun hitherward; then indeed they beheld their own vigorous self-sustenance.
(20.63.3.c) Through this [hymn], may we win god-ordained booty; may we rejoice for a hundred winters, blessed with brave sons.
3 (20.63.4’) He who alone bestows wealth upon the mortal who offers oblations—Indra, the sovereign and irresistible one, indeed. 4
When will he trample with his foot the stingy mortal like a mushroom?
When indeed will Indra truly listen to our songs?
For whoever, having pressed the soma, seeks to win you away from many [others]— 5 —
(20.63.6.c) That formidable power belongs to Śavas; Indra alone possesses it.
(20.63.7’) O most powerful Indra, we implore that exhilaration which is the greatest drinker of Soma, which is conscious, and by which you strike down the devouring demon.
(20.63.7.c) We seek that very [power] with which you slay the glutton.
We implore that [power] by which you protected Daśagva, Adhrigu, Vepayan, and Svarṇara; we implore that [power] by which you protected the ocean.
By which you urged on the Sindhu and the great waters like chariots.
We pray for that path so that we may travel upon the way of Truth.
O Indra, come to us! You are beloved, the ever-conquering, the unconcealable, broad on every side like a mountain, the Lord of Heaven.
For you, O true one, O drinker of Soma, have indeed encompassed both worlds;
O Indra, you are the strengthener of the presser of juice, the Lord of Heaven.
For you, O Indra, are the shatterer of eternal fortresses.
The slayer of the Dasyu, the prosperer of Manu, the Lord of Heaven. (3) O Adhvaryu, pour forth of this sweet, most intoxicating juice;
for thus is the Hero praised, he who ever prospers. (4)
O Indra, driver of the bay steeds, no one has ever reached your ancient praise with might, nor with songs of celebration. Seeking glory,
we have invoked that Lord of spoils for you.
(20.64.6.c) He who is to be magnified by sacrifices that do not fail in their purpose.
6 (20.65.1’) Come now, O friends, let us praise Indra, the hero worthy of hymns; (20.65.1.c) he who alone stands superior over all tribes. 1

To him who does not withhold the cow, who seeks the cow, the celestial one— to him speak a wondrous word sweeter than clarified butter and honey. To him whose heroic powers are immeasurable, and whose bounty is beyond reaching.
The sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*) surpasses all light.
Praise Indra like Vyaśva— him who is waveless, the prize-winner, the controller,
who bestows the wealth of the enemy upon the donor.
Thus now, O son of Vyaśva, praise the tenth and the ninth [Agni],
the one who is well-knowing and worthy of celebration by those who move upon the earth. For you, O wielder of the thunderbolt, know how to avoid the snares of destruction.
Day by day he becomes pure, like one who has crossed over pitfalls.
(3) For the one who presses the juice wins a dwelling place of abundance; for the one who presses indeed worships away his enemies—the enemies of the gods, away his enemies.
Pressing the juice, the prize-winner, unrestrained, seeks to win thousands. (1)
To the one who presses the soma, Indra gives enduring wealth; he gives enduring wealth.

May those manly deeds of yours never turn away from us; may your glories not decay, nor may our strongholds decay. Whatever wondrous, immortal sound of yours is ever new in age after age—[may that reach us].
O Maruts, bestow upon us that which is difficult to overcome, and maintain that which is difficult to overcome.

I honor Agni as the Hotṛ-priest, the bountiful, the Vasu, the Son of Strength, Jātavedas— the wise one like a sage, Jātavedas— who, a god of perfect sacrifice, approaches the gods with his upward-reaching form.
He desires the brilliance of the clarified butter, following the flame of the offered fat.
Blazing with their ornaments, mingled with sacrifices, with spotted deer-skins and spears, they take their course;
O bright ones, you who are dear to the ointments— Sitting upon the sacrificial grass, O sons of Bharata, O heroes of heaven, drink the Soma from the Potar’s cup!
(20.67.5) Bring the gods here, O sage; sacrifice and sit down, O Hotṛ, upon the three seats.
Accept the Soma-sweetness that has been set forth; drink from the Āgnīdhra-vessel and satisfy yourself with your portion.
(20.67.6) This indeed is for you, increasing the manliness of your body; it bestows strength upon your arms from of old.
(20.67.6.c) For you, O Maghavan, the pressed juice has been offered; for you it is brought. Drink of this from the Brāhmaṇa’s cup until you are satisfied.
(20.67.7’) Him whom I called upon before, him I call now; he indeed is to be invoked, he who is the giver and the master of the name.
O Draviṇodas, drink the Soma-sweetness set forth by the Adhvaryus from the Potṛ’s cup, according to the seasons.
We invoke day by day for our protection the one who fashions beautiful forms, like a well-milking cow for the milker.
O drinker of Soma, come to our libations and drink of the Soma!
(20.68.2.c) O Godā, this exhilaration is for the wealthy one.
||2|| (20.68.3’) Then may we find from you the most intimate of your favors;
(20.68.3.c) do not overlook us, but come to us! ||3||
Ask the wise Indra, who is unassailable by enemies,
he who is more excellent than your friends. And let our revilers say, "We have turned away from others."
(20.68.5.c) Offering worship to Indra alone.
||5|| (20.68.6’) And may the people, O Wondrous One, call us fortunate;
(20.68.6.c) may we abide in the protection of Indra. ||6||
Bring this [soma] for the swift one, the swiftest, which is the glory of the sacrifice and the delight of men;
flying forth, it gladdens its friend.
Having drunk of this, O Śatakratu, you became the slayer of the Vṛtras.
(20.68.8.c) Protect the prize-winner in the contests for booty.
(20.68.9.a) As such, O Śatakratu, we strengthen you, the prize-winner, in the contests for booty;
(20.68.9.c) O Indra, for the winning of riches.
To him who is a great source of wealth, easy to cross over, and the friend of the one who presses the soma—
to that Indra,
sing! Come here, sit down, and sing forth unto Indra.
(20.68.11.c) O friends, you who bring hymns of praise! ||11|| To Indra, the most abundant among the many, the lord of desirable treasures, at the pressed soma juice. ||12||

May he indeed come to us for our success; may he come for wealth and for inspired wisdom; may he come to us with spoils of war. He whose two bay steeds no enemies can restrain when they are harnessed in the midst of battles.
Sing for that Indra!
(20.69.2.c) For him, the drinker of the pressed juice, these pure Soma drops, mixed with curds, go forth to be enjoyed. (20.69.3.c) They flow as the pressed juices. (20.69.3.c) 3.
O Indra, most skillful in action, you were born to increase at once upon drinking the pressed juice for the sake of supreme sovereignty.
O Indra, lover of songs, let the swift Soma juices enter into you.
May they be auspicious for you, O wise one. The hymns have magnified you; the recitations have magnified you, O Lord of a hundred powers.
May our songs of praise magnify you.
May Indra, whose protection is imperishable, win for us this thousandfold prize,
in which all manly powers reside.
O Indra, lover of songs, let not mortals do harm to our bodies.
(20.69.8.c) May the Lord ward off the weapon.
(20.69.9.a) Those who stand around harness the ruddy, bright one as he moves;
(20.69.9.c) the luminaries shine in the sky.
They yoke his two beloved bay horses to the chariot on either side—
red, bold, carrying heroes.
Making a banner for the bannerless, a form for the formless, O men.

O Indra, with those who break even what is firm and with those who carry you as priests,
you found the ruddy cows even in the cave.
Like those seeking the gods according to their thought, our songs have gone forth toward you, the finder of wealth.
The great one has roared, the famous one.
||2|| For you shall be seen united with Indra, meeting with him who is fearless— you two, joyful, equal in splendor. ||3||
With blameless, radiant, and powerful hosts, he, the sacrifice,

To Indra alone the singers have sung aloud; to Indra, with hymns, the chanters;
to Indra the voices have cried out.
Indra indeed is joined with the two bay steeds, mingled with them, yoked by a word.
Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt, is golden.
8 Indra caused the sun to ascend to heaven for far-reaching vision;
he impelled Indra with the rays of light. 9
O Indra, protect us in battles for booty and in contests for a thousandfold prizes, you, the fierce one, with your fierce aids.
We invoke Indra in the great contest for wealth; we invoke Indra in the small one.
The wielder of the thunderbolt, our ally in battles against the Vṛtras. (11) O showerer of blessings, O ever-conquering one, open up that vessel for us, for us, you who are irresistible. (12)
At every clash, at every higher encounter, the hymns of Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt—
yet I find no adequate praise for him.
Like a bull among the herds, he drives the people forward with his might.
The sovereign, unopposed;
he who alone rules over the peoples, over the treasures,
Indra, over the five tribes.
We invoke Indra for you from all sides, away from other people;
may he be ours alone.
O Indra, [grant us] winning wealth, that which is victorious and ever-conquering.
Bring forth the most excellent [soma] for our protection!
17 By means of which, aided by you, we may strike down with our fists and hold back the Vṛtras with our horse. 18
O Indra, protected by you, may we take up the thunderbolt as a weapon;
may we utterly conquer our rivals in battle.
O Indra, with you as our ally, may we—through brave archers—be victorious.
May we overcome those who attack us. 20.70.20c Great indeed is Indra, and let there be even greater majesty for the wielder of the thunderbolt;
his power is as vast as the sky in its breadth. 20.71.1abc
Like the vast waters from the palate. For thus his bounty is overflowing, great, rich in cattle, like a branch laden with ripe fruit for the donor.
For thus indeed are thy powers and thy aids, O Indra, for one such as I;
they are instantly available to the donor.
For thus indeed are his desirable things: the hymn of praise and the recitation of the *uktha* are to be celebrated.
For Indra, for the drinking of Soma. (6) Come, O Indra, and exhilarate yourself with the juice through all the Soma-pressings;
you are great in might and a mighty helper. (7)
Pour this exhilarating juice for Indra, the exhilarating one;
pour it for the doer of all deeds, for the one who accomplishes everything.
O fair-cheeked one, lord of all people, be intoxicated by these exhilarating hymns of praise.
And at these libations, O Indra—(9) Your songs have been poured forth; they have risen up toward you, Like a bull, toward the unappeased Lord. (10)
Impel toward us a wondrous and choice gift, O Indra; may it be abundant and powerful for you. O Indra, impel us well therein toward wealth, making us zealous.
O thou of many splendors, [bestow] fame upon the illustrious one. O Indra, bestow upon us abundant and vast renown, consisting of cattle and booty;
grant us all-encompassing, imperishable life.
Bestow upon us great renown and splendor that wins a thousandfold;
O Indra, grant us those nourishments borne on chariots. Praising with songs the praiseworthy Indra, the lord of wealth, the master of riches—
(20.71.15.c) He goes to the oblation for our protection.
||15|| (20.71.16’) At every pressing, the pious man sings forth a great hymn of praise to Indra, who dwells at home. ||16||
For at all the libations, those who long for the bull urge you on—the one common to all, each separately, as they desire to win the light of heaven, each separately.
We set you, like a ship that carries us across, at the pole of our strength;
the Āyus awaken Indra with sacrifices, the Āyus awaken Indra with hymns of praise.
Couples seeking your aid have spread themselves out for you, O Indra, as they release their draughts to win the stall of cattle; may they prevail, O Indra, as they release their draughts.
When you bring together two people who seek cattle or who seek the light of heaven, you, O Indra, manifest your thunderbolt—the companion of the bull, the companion that accompanies you.
May he indeed take pleasure in this our dawn; be mindful of the hymn and the oblation through our invocations, through the invocations for the winning of the light.
O Indra, when you, the bull, the wielder of the thunderbolt, intend to slay the enemies, listen to this prayer of mine, of this most recent worshipper, listen to the prayer of this most recent one.
To you alone, O Hero, do I offer all these libations; for you I fashion these strengthening prayers.
You are to be invoked by men at all times.
O fierce one, O wonder-worker, even now no one attains the greatness of you who are so highly esteemed.
(20.73.2.c) Neither your valor, O Indra, nor your bounty [is surpassed].
(20.73.3’) Bring forth [hymns] for the great one who increases greatness; offer your devotion to the wise one. (20.73.3.c) Go forth to the many clans, O filler of the peoples!
When the gold-adorned thunderbolt and the chariot arrive, which the two bay steeds of Yama draw along with the patrons,
Maghavan, renowned from of old, Indra, the lord of far-famed booty, mounts it. Even he, Indra,
together with his own herd of rain-clouds, sprinkles his golden beard.
He seeks a good dwelling when the sweet juice is pressed; he shakes [the world] like the wind shaking the forest.

(5) We praise that very manly deed of his who with his word struck down many thousands of malevolent ones who speak discordantly and wickedly—he who, like a father, increased his own vigor and might. (6)
For even though we are, O truthful Soma-drinkers,
as if unpraised, O Indra, do you indeed grant us hope for a thousand beautiful cattle and horses, O Lord of abundant wealth!
O Siprín, Lord of spoils, Master of power, yours are wondrous deeds.
O Indra, most wealthy one, grant us a share of fair cattle, of horses, and of thousands!
Lull those who look at each other into sleep; let them lie down and not wake.
O Indra, most wealthy one, grant us a share of fair cattle, of horses, and of thousands!
May those enemies sleep; may the patrons, O Hero, wake!
O Indra, most wealthy one, grant us a share of a thousand beautiful horses and cattle!
O Indra, crush the braying donkey who bellows so loudly.
(20.74.5.c) O Indra, grant us a share indeed of beautiful cattle and horses, in thousands, O thou of abundant wealth!
(20.74.6’) Let the wind blow far away with the *kuṇḍṛṇācī* plant from the forest;
O Indra, grant us a share indeed of beautiful cattle and horses, in thousands, O thou of abundant wealth!
(20.74.7) Crush all clamor; destroy Kṛkadāśva!
O Indra, most wealthy one, grant us a share of a thousand beautiful cattle and horses!
(20.75.1) Couples seeking your aid have spread themselves out for you, O Indra, at the winning of the stall of cattle; they have come forth, they have come forth seeking you.

When you, O Indra, bring together the two peoples seeking cattle as they strive for the light of heaven, you thunder aloud, manifesting the bull-like, ever-present thunderbolt— your constant companion.
The Pūrus have known this heroic power of yours, O Indra, when you shattered the autumnal fortresses, overcoming them as you struck them down.
(20.75.2.c) O Indra, Lord of Might, you chastised that mortal who did not sacrifice;
(20.75.2.e) in your exhilaration, you stole away the great earth and these waters—these very waters.

2 (20.75.3’) Then indeed they celebrated this heroic deed of yours during the intoxications, O Bull, when you, the eager ones, helped those who sought your aid; when you helped those who were your friends.
(20.75.3.c) You performed this deed for them so that they might prevail in battles; (20.75.3.e) seeking glory, they won one river after another; seeking glory, they won them.
3 (20.76.1’) Like a wheel set upon a tree, your pure hymn of praise has awakened you two, O swift ones.

He for whom Indra is the Hotar-priest on many days—the protector of men, the most heroic among heroes, the lord of the night—(1) May we be foremost at the dawning of this morning and of the future one, O most heroic of heroes!
May Triśoka bring hither a hundred men with his chariot, which, having been victorious, was joined by Kutsa. (2)
(20.76.3) What exhilarating joy has been for you, O Indra? You, the fierce one, have opened wide the doors; let our songs flow forth toward you.
Why do you not come hither toward me with your thought? May I be able to bring you near with gifts and food.
(20.76.4) What splendor belongs to men like you, O Indra? With what intention will you act? Why have you not come to us?
Like Mitra, he is true, far-striding, for our sustenance, so that the inspired thoughts of everyone may find their fulfillment in food.
O Sūrya, drive us to our goal as if to the further shore; let those who have come to fulfill his desire go forth like bridegrooms.
And those men, O Indra of many births, who with offerings strive to win back your many songs of praise.
For you, O Indra, mother heaven is well-measured with her vastness, and earth with her poetic wisdom.
For your choice, let the pressed juices rich in ghee be sweet for your drinking; let the honeyed draughts be delicious.
They have poured out a full vessel of honey for this Indra, for he is truly bountiful.
He has grown great over the breadth of the earth, a hero among men, by his wisdom and manly deeds.
Indra, self-strong, has scattered the hostile armies; many strive for his friendship.
Ascend your chariot as if for battle, which you shall urge on with auspicious favor.
Let the true Maghavan, the drinker of the dregs, come hither; let his bay steeds run toward us.

For him we have pressed the soma-juice, most effective; being praised here, may he grant us his presence. O Hero, descend like one at the end of a journey, so that you may rejoice today at this our libation.

Like Uśanas, the wise ordainer shall proclaim the hymn; he shall offer a prayer to the conscious Asura. Like a seer, accomplishing the secret rites, when the bull, swelling with his flow, shall sing his praise, he will thus engender the seven singers from heaven; singing their songs, they have established the sacred ordinances even by day.

When the beautiful light of heaven was made manifest with hymns, they caused the great radiance to shine at the break of day; the most heroic one, in his assistance, has dispelled the blinding and turbid darkness so that men may see.
Indra, impetuous for the draught, has grown to immeasurable power; he has filled both worlds with his greatness.
Even beyond this, his majesty extends, he who has surpassed all worlds.
Śakra, knowing all manly deeds, released the waters with his longing companions—
those who by their words split even the rock and, as seekers, opened the stall filled with cattle.
You struck down Vṛtra who had obstructed the waters; the earth, in accord with you, aided your thunderbolt. You sent forth the oceanic floods; O bold hero, by your might you became their lord.
When you, O much-invoked one, shattered the rock and released the waters, Saramā appeared before you.

(20.77.8.c) As our leader, may you strike out abundant booty, shattering the cow-pens while being praised by the Aṅgirases. 8 (20.78.1’) Sing this for you when the soma is pressed, for the one invoked by many, the warrior, that which is as beneficial as a well for a powerful bull. 1
The Bounteous One does not withhold the gift of booty consisting of cattle,
once he has heard our songs.
May the slayer of the Dasyus surely come to this cow-filled stall of his.
(20.78.3.c) With your powers, open for us the way!
(20.79.1’) O Indra, bring us wisdom, just as a father provides for his sons. Teach us, O Much-invoked One, on this journey; living, may we attain the light.
Let not unknown, malevolent, or unpropitious strongholds step upon us.
With you, O Hero, may we cross over the eternal downward-flowing waters.
O Indra, bring to us the highest, most powerful, and fulfilling fame.
(20.80.1.c) O wondrous one, wielder of the thunderbolt, fair-cheeked god, by whom these two worlds, heaven and earth, have been filled.
(20.80.2’) O King, we invoke you, the fierce subduer of peoples among the gods, for our protection.
O Vasu, make all our wavering things firm; make our enemies easy to overcome.
O Indra, even if there were a hundred heavens and a hundred earths belonging to you,
O wielder of the thunderbolt, neither a thousand suns nor the two worlds could equal you at your birth.
You have filled all things with your greatness and your dark power, O bull, most mighty one, by your strength.
(20.81.2.c) O Maghavan, wielder of the thunderbolt, protect us with your wondrous aids in the cattle-filled stall.
(20.82.1’) O Indra, if I were the master of as much wealth as you possess, I would surely provide for my praiser; O dispenser of riches, I would not leave him to misery.
Day by day may I learn to magnify you, so that wealth may be found wherever it is;
for there is no kinship better than yours, O Maghavan—not even a father.
O Indra, [grant] a triple-layered refuge, a threefold protection, full of well-being.

Grant protection to the liberal patrons and to me; ward off the missile from them. Those who, with minds intent on cattle, have overcome the enemy and strike him down boldly—O Indra, Maghavan, lover of songs, be our closest protector of our bodies.
O Indra, come, O you of wondrous luster; these pressed juices long for you, purified through the fine strainer in a continuous stream.
O Indra, come, impelled by our prayer and urged by the sages, to the one who has prepared the soma.
(20.84.2.c) Toward the sacred hymns, O priest!
(20.84.3’) O Indra, come hither with haste toward the sacred hymns, O Lord of the Bay Steeds; take pleasure in our pressed soma.
(20.85.1) Do not praise anything else, O friends; do not suffer harm.
Praise Indra alone, the bull, when the soma is pressed; recite your hymns repeatedly.
(20.85.2) [Praise him who is] like a rushing bull, unaging, a subduer of peoples, like a cow.
(20.85.2.c) Causing enmity, effecting reconciliation, bringing about both [results], most bountiful, and winning both sides.
(20.85.3’) For although these people here invoke you in various ways for aid, O Indra, let this our prayer be your strengthener through all the days.
(20.85.3.c) Let this our prayer, O Indra, be your strengthener through all the days.
The inspired singers of the noble folk, O Maghavan, vie with one another in their hymns.
Approach and bring us strength in many forms, most near for our protection.
With a prayer joined by prayer, I yoke for you the two bay steeds, your companions, swift and reveling together at the feast.
(20.86.1.c) Mounting the firm and comfortable chariot, O Indra, approach the Soma with knowledge as one who is wise.
(20.87.1’) O Adhvaryus, offer the reddish-milked stalk to the bull of the peoples!
Indra, seeking him, goes day after day from the cow-stall to the more familiar drinking-place, desiring the pressed Soma.
The lovely food which you have held from of old, day by day you desire its drinking;
O Indra, rejoicing in heart and mind, desiring them, drink the pressed Soma juices that stand before you.
Having been born, you drank the Soma for the sake of power; your mother proclaimed your greatness.
O Indra, you have filled the wide mid-air; through battle, you have created ample space for the gods.

When you fought against those who considered themselves great, we overcame them as they boasted with their arms; or when, O Indra, surrounded by men, you went forth to battle—may we, through you, win that glorious contest.
I shall proclaim the first deeds of the Bounteous One, and those new ones which he has performed.
When he overcame the godless illusions, then Soma became his own alone.
This entire world of cattle all around belongs to you—whatever you behold with the eye of the Sun.
(20.87.6.c) You are the sole lord of cattle, O Indra; may we enjoy the wealth that you have bestowed.
(20.87.7’) O Bṛhaspati and Indra, you two are the masters of celestial and terrestrial wealth. Bestow riches even upon the humble singer who praises you; protect us always with your blessings.
Bṛhaspati, who with his roar has suddenly propped apart the ends of the earth, he who dwells in the three stations—
him the ancient seers, the inspired singers, meditating, have placed before them, him whose tongue is delightful.
O Bṛhaspati, those who, as shakers of the world, rejoicing in their excellent wisdom, have assailed us.
The speckled, flowing, inviolable, wide expanse—O Bṛhaspati, protect its source!
O Bṛhaspati, from that furthest distance, those who touch the cosmic order have sat down before you;
for you, the wells dug out and milked by the stones drip honey all around in abundance.
Bṛhaspati, being born first from the great light in the highest heaven,
he who was many-born with seven mouths, blew away the darknesses with his roar and his seven rays.
With his well-praising, hymn-singing host, he shattered Vala, the enclosure, with his roar.
Bṛhaspati, bellowing loudly, drove forth the lowing, ruddy cows that sweeten the oblation.
(5) Thus let us serve the Father, the bull who belongs to all the gods, with sacrifices, homage, and offerings.
O Bṛhaspati, may we, possessing good offspring and heroic sons, become masters of riches. (6)
Even as one who shoots his arrow at dawn, bring forth this hymn for him like one adorning himself.
O sages, cross over the speech of the enemy with your own voice; O singer, cause Indra to settle down upon the Soma. Win over the cow with your milking; O singer, awaken your friend, the lover Indra.
Empty out the treasury that is not full of wealth; bring forth the hero for the sake of giving bounty!
(20.89.2) Why indeed, O Maghavan, do they call you a liberal giver? Sharpen me; I hear that you are one who sharpens.
O Śakra, let my prayer be effective; O Indra, bring us fortune that finds wealth! (20.89.3)
O Indra, people standing together in battle call upon you in their desire for possessions.

In this matter, the hero makes him his ally who brings oblations; he does not desire friendship with one who presses no soma. He who, providing nourishment, presses sharp-edged soma juices for him in abundance, like trembling wealth—‖4‖
For him, he makes his enemies eager for flight at the break of dawn; he strikes down Vṛtra with his own hand.
(5) In that Indra we place our hope—Maghavan, who has fixed his desire upon us—even though he be far away, let his enemy tremble; let all human glories bow down before him. (6)
Drive the enemy far away with that fierce *śamba* weapon, O you who are invoked by many!
Bestow upon us wealth consisting of barley and cattle, O Indra; grant the singer a prayer rich in booty.
Into whom the strong-pressed, sharp Somas with abundant ends enter during the race—Indra...
Maghavan does not withhold the gift; he bestows abundant wealth upon the one who presses the soma.
(8) Furthermore, as a superior gambler wins the stake, so the one who desires the gods does not withhold his wealth; like a skilled thrower of the dice, he distributes it at the proper time.
He who desires the gods does not obstruct his riches; indeed, he pours forth wealth for him by his own inherent powers. (9)
O Much-invoked One, may we overcome ill-will with cattle, or hunger with barley, O All-pervading One!
May we, unhurt, be the first among kings to win riches through our strongholds.
May Bṛhaspati protect us from behind, and from above, and from below against the wicked.

May Indra from the front and from the middle grant us, his friends, a wider space for our friendship. Bṛhaspati, the breaker of the rock, the first-born, the upholder of Truth, the descendant of Aṅgiras, rich in oblations, with his double stride, seated at the morning sacrifice as our father— the Bull— roars aloud to the two worlds, heaven and earth.

Bṛhaspati, who has indeed created a wide space for such a person as he at the invocation of the gods—he slaying the Vṛtras, shatters the fortresses; he conquers his enemies and overcomes his adversaries in battles. Bṛhaspati, this god, has won all treasures and the great stalls full of cattle.
Desiring to win the waters and the light, Bṛhaspati, irresistible, slays the enemy with his hymns.
Our father discovered this seven-headed, lofty prayer, born of Eternal Order (*ṛta*).
Ayāsya, the friend of all people, generating the fourth [stanza], recited the hymn for Indra.

Proclaiming the *ṛta*, meditating on the straight path, the sons of Dyaus, the heroes of the Asura, the Aṅgirases— placing the inspired sage in their station— conceived the first foundation of the sacrifice.
Like swans with their clamoring companions, they cast aside the stone-made bonds.
Bṛhaspati, bellowing toward the cows, praised them and, knowing [the way], sang aloud.
(3) With two [steps] he drove them down, with one he drove them away—the cows standing hidden behind the dam of falsehood.
Bṛhaspati, seeking light in the darkness, drove the ruddy cows out; for he disclosed the three [hidden] ones. (4)

Having shattered the fortress, he drove it away to the west; Bṛhaspati cut open the three [fortresses] together from the ocean. He found the Dawn, the Sun, the Cow, and the Light, thundering like the sky.
Indra, with a roar, split Vala—the guardian of the milch-cows—as if with his hand.
(20.91.6.c) Seeking the milk-mixture with sweating hands and ointments, he made the Paṇi weep; he stole away the cows.

(20.91.7’) With his true, glowing companions, the winners of wealth, he rent asunder the one who held the cattle. Brahmaṇaspati, with his bull-like boars sweating from the heat, attained the treasure.
Seeking cattle with a truthful mind, they impelled the Lord of Cattle with their prayers.
Bṛhaspati, with those who avert mutual reproach and who yoke themselves, released the ruddy cows.
Increasing him with auspicious hymns, like a lion roaring in his dwelling place—

(20.91.9.c) May we rejoice after Bṛhaspati, the bull, the victorious one, in every battle for the sake of heroes. (20.91.10’) When he won the prize of all forms and ascended to heaven, to the highest dwellings— then,
strengthening the bull Bṛhaspati, though being many, they bore the light with their mouths.
Make true our prayer for the bestowing of vital strength; for you protect even the lowly singer with your own inherent ways.
Let all adversaries fall behind us; hear this, O Heaven and Earth, you who encompass all things!
Indra, by his greatness, split asunder the head of the vast surging ocean, of Arbuda.
He slew the serpent and set the seven rivers free; O Heaven and Earth, together with the gods, protect us!
Sing forth with song to Indra, the lord of cattle, even as he is known:
the begetter of truth, the protector of the righteous.
The bay steeds have been let loose upon the ruddy sacrificial grass,
where we raise our voices together in song.
For Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt, the cows have yielded the milk-mixture, the honeyed draught.

(20.92.3.c) That which he found in the secret place. (20.92.4’) When we two, Indra and I, go up to the dwelling-place on the ridge of the sun, having drunk of the honeyed draught, let us dwell together in the three-times-seven places of our friend. Sing praise, sing it forth; O Priyamedhas, sing your praise!
Let even the young children sing; sing boldly as if for a fortress!
(5) The gargara-shell shall sound downward, and the lizard shall croak all around.
The tawny one has roared around; a prayer has been raised for Indra.
When the dappled cows, easy to milk and unflinching, come running hither—seize the unflinching Soma for Indra to drink.
Indra has drunk, Agni has drunk; all the gods have become exhilarated.
Varuṇa indeed dwells here; toward him the waters have lowed, like mother cows toward their calf.
(8) You are a good god, O Varuṇa, you to whom the seven rivers belong.
They flow toward the palate like [water] toward a hollowed-out sun.
He who made the well-yoked steeds leap forward for the donor— he is the swift leader, that very wondrous form who was released as the highest.
Truly, O Śakra, Indra has overcome all enemies;
he split apart the child’s porridge as it was cooking beyond the mountain with his song.
Like a small boy, he stood upon the chariot-pole.
He [brought] a winged buffalo and a deer for his father and mother, he of far-reaching power. (12) O fair-cheeked lord of the house, mount your golden chariot!
Then let us two accompany the celestial, thousand-footed, ruddy, well-faring, and peerless [steed]. (13)
To him indeed, the self-radiant one, the worshipful ones sit down;
they turn toward his well-placed purpose so that he may come hither to bestow gifts.
Following the ancient dwelling of these Priyamedhas— 14–15 —

Following the ancient practice, those who have spread the sacrificial grass and prepared the offerings have attained [the gods]. He who is the king of the peoples, who moves with his chariots unrestrained,
the overcomer of all hostile armies— he is praised as the eldest Vṛtra-slayer.
O Puruhanman, glorify that Indra for his protection, in whose hand, as the distributor,
the beautiful thunderbolt was placed from of old, like the great sun in the sky. No one shall equal him in deed who has made him ever-increasing.
Like Indra, who is praised by all with sacrifices—the skillful, the unassailable, the one of daring might;
(18) The invincible, the fierce, the conqueror in battles—he at whose birth the great, far-reaching milch-cows lowed together, and the heavens and the earths lowed. (19)
O Indra, even if there were a hundred heavens and a hundred earths belonging to you,
O wielder of the thunderbolt, neither a thousand suns nor both worlds could equal you at your birth.
You have filled [all things] with your greatness and manly power, O bull, most mighty one, by your strength.
(20.92.21.c) O Maghavan, help us with your wondrous aids, O wielder of the thunderbolt, to a stall full of cattle.
‖21‖ (20.93.1’) May the hymns of praise exhilarate you; bestow bounty, O Lord of the Stone; strike down those who hate sacred prayer. ‖1‖
Trample underfoot those who are stingy and ungenerous; you are great.
For no one at all can withstand you.
(20.93.3) You, O Indra, are the master of the pressed juices, and you are the master of the unpressed.

(20.93.3.c) You are the king of the people. (20.93.4’) Swinging themselves about, the active ones wait upon Indra at his birth, having obtained excellent heroic power. O Indra, you were born from strength, from power, and from might;
O bull, you are indeed a bull.
O Indra, you are the slayer of Vṛtra; you have extended across the mid-air.
(20.93.6.c) You propped up the sky with your might. ||6|| (20.93.7.a) O Indra, you bear the hymn in harmony with [the gods] within your arms;
(20.93.7.c) sharpening the thunderbolt with your might. ||7||
(20.93.8) O Indra, you are the conqueror of all beings by your might; as such, you have pervaded all worlds.
8 (20.94.1) Let Indra, the lord of the self, come for exhilaration—he who, powerful and impetuous, hastens according to the cosmic law. 1
(20.94.1.c) Surpassing all powers of resistance with his boundless and mighty virility;
(20.94.2’) Well-seated is your chariot, well-governed are your two bay steeds; O Lord of Men, the thunderbolt is fixed in your hand.
(20.94.2.c) Come hither quickly, O King, by a fair path; we shall increase your manly powers as you drink.

Let the fierce and powerful ones, borne by Indra’s steeds, bring hither to us this king with the thunderbolt in his arm— the fierce, the mighty, the vigorous bull of true strength, our companion in the feast. Thus, O Bull,
you hasten toward the master who dwells in the wooden vat, the wise one, the pillar of vigor, the supporter of the world.
(20.94.4.c) Display your vigor; gather it within you, so that you may be the lord for the increase of those who drink with the *kenipa* vessel.
(20.94.5.a) May riches come to us, for I have praised you; come to the bearer of the well-prayed blessing, to the one who possesses the Soma.
(20.94.5.c) You are the master; sit down upon this sacred grass (*barhis*), for by your law your vessels are inviolable.
The first invocations of the gods went forth separately; they performed deeds for glory that were difficult to surpass.
Those who were unable to board the sacrificial ship—like cripples—they sank down in despair.
Thus indeed let the others, the malicious ones, go away—their horses are yoked to ill-fitting yokes.
(20.94.7.c) Thus, those who were previously below are now present for the giving, where there are many provisions and means of enjoyment.
(20.94.8.a) He has firmly established the mountains and the plains as they trembled; Heaven thundered and shook the mid-air regions.
(20.94.8.c) He props apart the two joined worlds; having drunk of the strong draught, he utters hymns of praise in his exhilaration.
I carry this well-fashioned goad for you, O Maghavan, with which you shall strike down those who damage the hooves [of our cattle].
May there be a welcome place for you at this libation; O Maghavan, be present as a sharer in the pressed juice and the sacrifice.
O Much-invoked One, may we cross over ill-will with cattle, and all hunger with barley.
(20.94.10.c) May we, together with the kings and our own heroic band, be the first to win riches.
(20.94.11’) May Bṛhaspati protect us from behind, and from above, and from below against the evildoer; may Indra from the front and from the middle, as a friend to his friends, grant us wide space.
(20.94.11.c) May Indra from the front and from the middle, as a friend to his friends, grant us wide space.

At the Trikadruka festivals, the mighty and impetuous buffalo drank his fill of the barley-mixed Soma pressed by Viṣṇu, according to his desire. It exhilarated him for the sake of performing great deeds; it followed him—the great and wide one. Thus the true drop attended upon the god Indra, the true god.
Sing forth this song of praise to this Indra, whose chariot is foremost!
Even in the encounter, the maker of space in the clash of battles, the slayer of Vṛtra—be our inspirer! May the bowstrings of our adversaries snap upon their bows!
You released the rivers to flow downward; you slew the serpent.

(20.95.3.c) O Indra, you were born without an enemy; you nourish every desirable thing. We embrace you; let the bowstrings of our adversaries snap upon their bows! ‖3‖ (20.95.4’) May all hostilities be utterly dispersed; may the prayers of the noble one reach us!
(20.95.4.c) Cast down the weapon upon the enemy who seeks to slay us, O Indra; let that gift of yours which bestows wealth be ours.
(20.95.4.e) May the bowstrings of our adversaries snap upon their bows!
4 (20.96.1’) Drink of this strong, invigorating draught; unyoke your two bay horses here along with all your chariot.

(20.96.1.c) O Indra, let not other sacrificers detain you; these pressed juices are for you alone. (20.96.2’) For you they have been pressed, and for you they are yet to be pressed; our strengthening songs call upon you. O Indra, enjoying this libation today, you who know all things, drink the Soma here.
Whosoever, desiring the gods, presses the Soma for him with longing mind and with his whole heart—for him Indra does not give up his cattle; he makes that [Soma] praised and lovely for him.
He is clearly seen by this [Indra]: he who, though wealthy, does not press the Soma for him.
(20.96.4.c) Maghavan places him beyond the reach of the cubit; he slays the haters of sacred knowledge without being commanded.
(20.96.5’) Desiring horses, desiring cattle, desiring booty, we call upon you to come near. Seeking to abide in your new favor, O Indra, may we invoke you for our welfare.
I release you by means of this oblation so that you may live, from unknown consumption as well as from royal consumption.
If the *grāhi* has seized him, O Indra and Agni, release him from her!
Whether his life-span is exhausted, or whether he has departed, or whether he has been brought into the very presence of Death—
I bring him forth from the lap of Destruction, untouched by harm, for a hundred autumns.
With an oblation that has a thousand eyes, a hundred powers, and a hundredfold life, I have brought him back.
May Indra lead him through the autumns to the further shore of every misfortune.
Live a hundred autumns, increasing in strength; live a hundred winters and a hundred springs.
May Indra, Agni, Savitṛ, and Bṛhaspati grant you a hundred years; with this oblation of a hundredfold life, I have brought him back.
I have brought you back, I have found you; you have returned, renewed once more.
(20.96.10.c) O you who are complete in all limbs, I have found your entire sight and your entire life.
(20.96.11’) May Agni, in accord with Brahmā, the slayer of demons, drive away from here (20.96.11.c) the disease that, having a wicked name, has settled within your womb and your birthplace.
Whatever disease of evil name has settled upon your embryo or your womb—
Agni, together with the sacred prayer (*brahman*), has driven that flesh-eater away.
Whatever [disease] kills what is falling, what is sitting still, or what is crawling—
(20.96.13.c) Him who seeks to destroy what has been born for you, him we cause to perish from here.
(20.96.14.a) He who spreads apart your thighs, who lies between husband and wife;
(20.96.14.c) he who licks the interior of the womb—him we cause to perish from here.
(20.96.15) That one who, having been your brother, or having become your husband, or having become your lover, lies with you;
that one who seeks to destroy your offspring—him we cause to perish from here.
(20.96.16) That one who lies with you after having deluded you with sleep and darkness.
(20.96.16.c) Him who seeks to destroy your offspring, him we cause to perish from here.
(20.96.17’) From your two eyes, from your two nostrils, from your two ears, and from your chin;
(20.96.17.c) the consumption (*yakṣma*) in your head, from your brain and from your tongue—I tear it away from you.
From your neck, from your *uṣṇihā* joints, from your vertebrae, and from your spine—
(18) I tear away from you the consumption (*yakṣma*) located in your shoulders, from your shoulder-blades, and from your arms.
(19) We tear away from you the consumption from your kidneys, from your spleen, and from your liver.
From your intestines, from your bowels, from the large intestine and from the belly;
from both your sides and from the bladder, from the navel, I tear away your *yakṣma* disease.
From your two thighs, from your two knees, from your two heels, and from your two foreparts of the feet.

The wasting disease from the anus, from the hips, from the buttocks, and from the flesh— I tear it away from you. From the penis, from the organ of pleasure, from your body hairs, and from your nails—
this wasting disease from your entire self, that I tear away from you.

(20.96.21.e) With my two hands, from your fingers and from your nails, I pull out the consumption. (20.96.21’) From every limb, from every hair, from every pore, and from every joint—(20.96.21.c) that consumption which is in your skin, we pull it out in all directions with the *vībarha* of Kaśyapa. (20.96.21’) We pull it out in all directions.
Depart, O Lord of the Mind; go away, O Desire, and move far off!
Look toward Nirṛti; let the mind of the living man turn in many directions.
We have indeed now caused this wielder of the thunderbolt to swell here with strength.
Therefore, bring today the Soma pressed alike for him; now indeed, attend upon the Glorious One.
Even Vṛka, the wild beast that crushes the breast, shall attend to his ordinances.
So, O Indra, come to this our hymn, graciously accepting it with wondrous thought.
(20.97.3) What manly deed of this Indra remains yet undone? By what glory has the slayer of Vṛtra not been heard of from his very birth?
(20.98.1) For it is you alone that we poets invoke for the winning of booty.
(20.98.1.c) O Indra, lord of the virtuous, men call upon you among the Vṛtras; they call upon you in the races of the steeds.

(20.98.2’) Therefore, O wonderful one, wielder of the thunderbolt, being boldly praised by us, O lord of the stone-pressed soma, scatter for us cattle and chariot-horses, O Indra—bestow them all like booty upon a victor.

(20.99.1) Toward you, O Indra, for the first draught, the Āyus with their hymns of praise, the Ṛbhus gathered together, and the Rudras have raised their voices in song, extolling the one who was first.
(20.99.2) In the exhilaration of this pressed juice, Indra has increased his manly strength and power within the wide expanse of Viṣṇu.
(20.99.2.c) Today, as in former times, men praise that majesty of his.
(20.100.1’) For now, O Indra, lover of songs, we have released our great desires toward you,
like those going upward with water.
O Hero, the sacred hymns increase you with their youthful strains,
even as you grow day by day,
O wielder of the stone. They harness the two bay steeds of the impetuous one to the broad-yoked chariot with the song.
(20.100.3.c) The two who carry Indra, yoked by our word.
||3|| (20.101.1’) We choose Agni as the messenger, the invoker, the all-knowing, the skillful performer of this sacrifice. ||1||
With invocations, they ever call upon Agni, Agni, the lord of the people,
the bearer of oblations, the one beloved by many.
O Agni, being born, bring the gods here for him who has strewn the sacrificial grass.
(20.101.3.c) You are our Hotṛ, worthy of praise.
(20.102.1’) Worthy of praise, worthy of homage, visible even through the darkness, Agni, the bull, is kindled. (20.102.1.c) 1.
Agni, the bull, is kindled like a horse that carries the gods;
him, the possessors of oblations worship.
O Bull, we who are bulls ourselves kindle you, the Bull.
(20.102.3.c) O Agni, shine forth mightily! ||3|| (20.103.1’) Invoke Agni with songs for protection, him whose flame is fierce;
(20.103.1.c) invoke Agni, O Purumīḷha, the famous one, for wealth; the men [invoke] Agni for a well-shining dwelling. ||1||
O Agni, come with the fires; we choose you as the Hotṛ-priest.
Let the extended ladle, full of oblation, anoint you, the most excellent sacrificer, to sit upon the sacrificial grass. For toward you, O Aṅgiras, son of strength, the ladles move at the sacrifice.
(20.103.3.c) We seek Agni, the Son of Strength, whose hair is clarified butter, the foremost in sacrifices.
(20.104.1’) O Lord of abundant wealth, may these songs of mine exalt you;
the wise ones, pure and bright as fire, have celebrated you with hymns of praise.
This one, made mighty by a thousand seers, has spread out like the ocean.
True is that greatness of his; his power is celebrated at the sacrifices in the kingdom of the inspired poets.
May Indra, who is to be invoked in all battles, be present for us.
(20.104.3.c) To the Vṛtra-slayer, the supreme conqueror, worthy of praise, come the sacred prayers and the libations.
3 (20.104.4.a) You are the first giver of riches; you are the true one who acts as a sovereign lord.
4 (20.104.4.c) We choose the alliance of the son of great power, of the one possessed of abundant splendor. 4
O Indra, in your onrushings you prevail over all rival hosts; you are the slayer of the accursed, the progenitor, the conqueror of all. You are the one who overcomes those who seek to overcome us.
The two worlds follow after your surging might, as two mother cows follow their youngling.

(20.105.2.c) All your rivals were struck down by your wrath when you, O Indra, overcame Vṛtra. (20.105.3’) From here [I call] for your aid that ageless one, the striker who is never struck back; the swift victor, the hurler, the best of chariot-warriors, the unsubdued one who strengthened Tugra’s son. Him who is the king of the people, the irresistible mover with his chariots,
the overcomer of all hostile armies, the eldest, the slayer of Vṛtra—
him, Indra, O Puruhanman, do thou glorify for protection, he whose support is twofold in the distributor of wealth.
(20.105.5.c) The beautiful thunderbolt has been placed in his hand, like the great sun in the sky.
5 (20.106.1’) That lofty power of yours, O Indra, your strength and your will— The *dhiṣaṇā* sharpens the desirable thunderbolt. 1
O Indra, heaven increases your manly power, and the earth increases your renown;
the waters and the mountains urge you on.
Viṣṇu, the lofty dwelling, Mitra, and Varuṇa sing your praises.
The host of Maruts exults after you.
(20.106.3.c) All the tribes, all the Kuṣṭayas, bow down before his wrath, as rivers flow toward the ocean. (20.107.1)
His vital power blazed forth when Indra rolled together both worlds like two skins.
With his hundred-knotted thunderbolt, he struck down even the fiercely shaking Vṛtra.
He split the head with the *vṛṣṇi* [thunderbolt].
This indeed was the eldest in all the worlds, from which the fierce one of brilliant valor was born.
As soon as he was born, he overcomes his enemies, when all his helpers rejoice after him.
Increasing in power and possessing abundant strength, he, as an enemy, instills fear in the Dāsa.
Winning both the unexpressed and the expressed, they cry out to you at the offerings during the exhilarations of the soma.
In you they pour forth their many mental powers, when these helpers become twice or thrice [in number].
(20.107.6.c) With the sweet, make it sweeter; with the sweet, join that [sweetness] together. Fight well against that with honey, [making it] most honey-sweet.

(20.107.7’) If indeed the inspired singers rejoice after you as you win riches in battle after battle, then, O mighty one, exert yourself with greater strength and firmness; let not the evil-minded Kaśoka-slayers harm you.
Through you we have confidence in battles, beholding many things worthy of war.
I urge on your weapons with my words; I sharpen your vital powers with sacred prayer.
You bestow that [gift] both upon the lower and the higher, in whichever house you have granted protection with your aid.

(20.107.9.c) Set up the swift-moving Mother; then set in motion many heroic deeds. (20.107.10’) Praise him who is vast in stature, possessed of many paths, the skillful one, the most powerful, the Aptya among the Aptyas. 11. O Brahman, let Bṛhaddiva, the son of Agni and winner of the light, perform this strengthening hymn for Indra.
As a self-ruling king, he governs over the great stall of cattle; though swift and fervent, he consumes everything like a surging ocean.
12. Thus has the great Bṛhaddiva Atharvan spoken: his own body is indeed Indra himself.
The two sisters dwelling in the mother [the dawn], free from blemish, impel them with power and cause them to grow strong.
(12) The brilliant banner of the gods, the radiant face, Sūrya rises toward the quarters.
The maker of day, with his splendors, has overcome the darkness; the pure one has crossed over all misfortunes. (13)
The brilliant face of the gods has risen, the eye of Mitra, Varuṇa, and Agni.
It has filled heaven, earth, and the intermediate space; Sūrya is the soul of all that moves and stands.
Sūrya approaches the radiant goddess Uṣas from behind, as a young man approaches a maiden.

(20.107.15.c) Where men seeking the gods extend their generations toward auspiciousness for the sake of the auspicious; ||15|| (20.108.1’) O Indra, bring to us strength and manly vigor, O Śatakratu, O far-seeing one;
[bring] a hero who conquers in battle. ||1||
For you indeed, O Vasu, have become our father; you, O Śatakratu, have become our mother.
Therefore, we seek your favor.
O impetuous one, much-invoked Śatakratu, I address you who are eager for the prize.
Grant us, O Lord, great heroic strength!
From this very center of the sweet honeyed draught, the Gaurī cows drink;
they who, moving in company with the bull Indra, rejoice for the sake of splendor—excellent ones, according to their own sovereignty.
Seeking him with longing, those dappled cows mix the Soma for him;
Indra’s dear milch-cows urge on his bolt, his missile, according to their own excellent sovereignty.
With reverence, those wise ones honor his conquering power.
(20.109.3.c) Many vows have followed him for his primordial perception; may the excellent ones [follow] his self-sovereignty.
3 (20.110.1’) For Indra, the exhilarated one, let our songs resound around the pressed juice; let the poets sing the hymn of praise. 1
In whom all glories rejoice, in the seven assemblies—
Indra we invoke when the soma is pressed.
At the Trikadruka rites, the gods performed the sacrifice that awakens the spirit.
May our songs of praise increase him.
Whether, O Indra, you rejoice in Soma with Viṣṇu, or with Trita Āptya,
or whether you delight among the Maruts with the drops— [we call upon you].

Or if, O Śakra, you rejoice in the distance or upon the ocean, take delight only in our pressed juice together with the drops. Or if you are the strengthener of the sacrificer who pours the libation, O Lord of the True, [rejoice in ours].
Or when you take delight in his hymn together with the drops.
Whatever has risen today, O Vṛtra-slayer, toward the sun—
O Indra, all that is under your control.
Or rather, O Lord of the Good, that you, having grown great, think "I shall not die"—
even that is indeed true for you.
Those Soma juices, whether pressed in the distance or pressed nearby—
(20.112.3.c) To all of them you go, O Indra.
(20.113.1.a) May Indra hear both [of us] here, this word directed toward him;
(20.113.1.c) may the most powerful Maghavan come with his focused thought for the drinking of the Soma.
For the two worlds have fashioned him as a self-ruling bull for the sake of power;
moreover, you sit as the foremost among those who are compared, for your mind is desirous of Soma.
O Indra, by your very birth from of old, you have been without a rival, without kin, and without a friend.
In battle you seek the friendship of your kin. (1) You do not find the wealthy man for friendship; the drunken ones despise you, O Surāśva.
When you make yourself a roaring bull and gather [the hosts] together, then indeed you are invoked like a father. (2)
For here from my father I have grasped the wisdom of the Eternal Order;
I have been born like Sūrya.
With an ancient thought, I adorn my songs as Kaṇva did.
By which Indra has indeed gained strength.
(2) O Indra, those seers who have not praised you, and those who have praised you— increase for me alone, being well-praised. (3)
O Indra, let us not be like outcasts or like strangers to you;
O wielder of the stone, we have thought ourselves like forests abandoned to decay, being difficult to satisfy. O slayer of Vṛtra, we have indeed thought ourselves slow and lacking in strength.
(20.116.2.c) O Hero, through your great bounty we have well performed our hymn of praise; may we rejoice.
(20.117.1’) Drink the Soma, O Indra; let it exhilarate you—the one which the stone, O Lord of Bay Steeds, has pressed for you, well-guided by the arms of the presser like a racing steed.
That exhilarating draught of yours which is yoked and lovely, by which you slay the Vṛtras, O Lord of the Bay Steeds—
let that intoxicate you, O Indra, Lord of abundant wealth.
Take heed well, O Maghavan, of this speech of mine, this hymn of praise which Vasiṣṭha recites for you.
(20.117.3.c) O Brahman, enjoy these at our common feast!
‖3‖ (20.118.1’) O Indra, Lord of Might, may you indeed prevail with all your aids; for we follow you, O Hero, as we would follow Bhaga—the glorious one who finds wealth. ‖1‖
(20.118.2) You are the first possessor of horses, the multiplier of cattle; O God, you are a golden spring.
(20.118.2c) For no one can exhaust the gift within you; whatever I ask of you, bring that here!

(20.143.3.c) May he who offers homage, directing his thought toward the ancient lover of the *ṛta*,
O Nāsatyas, you who exist in many places, come to this sacrifice on your golden chariot;
drink of the honeyed Soma and bestow treasure upon the person who honors you.
Come to us from heaven and from earth on your well-rolling golden chariot.

(20.143.5.c) Let not other seekers of the gods restrain you two, since your ancient kinship has been established. (20.143.6’) Now, O wonder-workers, measure out for us great wealth consisting of many heroes among both our parties;
when the men of the Ajas and the Amīḷhas have come to offer praise to you, O Aśvins, they have joined in the common laud.
Whatever I have here on earth asked of you both together, may that be for us a benevolent favor, O you who possess wealth as a prize.
Protect the singer; for our desire is fixed upon you both, O Nāsatyas.
May the plants be full of sweetness, the heavens and the waters; may the mid-air be sweet for us.
May the Lord of the Field be sweet for us; may we follow him unharmed.
(8) O Aśvins, that deed of yours is worthy of praise: the bull [of yours] from heaven, the mid-air, and the earth.
The thousand praises and those [deeds] in the search for cattle—all these you have come to drink. (9)
